In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-A'raf

The Shaykh, the Imam, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Know that Surah al-A'raf is Meccan, except for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And ask them about the town which was by the sea﴾ up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾. This portion was revealed in Medina. It has been related that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited in the Maghrib prayer "the longer of the two longs" (tul al-tulayn), meaning Surah al-A'raf. It was called "the longer of the two longs" because the longest surahs revealed in Mecca are Surah al-An'am and Surah al-A'raf, and al-A'raf is the longer of the two.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Alif. Lam. Mim. Sad.﴾ Its meaning: Allah knows best and makes distinct. It was also said: its meaning is "I am Allah, the True King." Al-Sha'bi said: every book has a secret, and the secret of the Qur'an is the disjoined letters at the beginnings of the surahs.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 2:

﴿A Book revealed to you﴾ Al-Farra' (al-Farra' [d. 207 AH], the grammarian) said: its construction is: "This is a Book revealed to you." ﴿So let there be no constriction in your breast about it﴾ meaning: doubt. The address is to the Messenger, and the community is also intended.

Al-ḥaraj (ḥaraj: constriction, narrowness) is in the sense of doubt, as al-Farra' said, and they cited the verse of poetry:

(Had it not been for doubt that blames me... I would have come to you to raid you, and you would not raid me.)

It was also said: al-ḥaraj is narrowness, and its meaning is: let your breast not be constricted in conveying (the message). That is because when the Prophet was sent to the disbelievers, he said: "O Lord, I fear that they will crush my head and make it like a piece of bread." So Allah the Exalted said: "Let there be no narrowness in your breast regarding the conveying, for I am your guardian and your helper."

His saying: ﴿That you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers﴾ contains inversion and reordering, and the construction of the verse is: "A Book revealed to you, that you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers, so let there be no constriction in your breast about it."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾. He means: the Qur'an. It was also said: the Qur'an and the Sunnah, by the command of Allah, exalted is He, because Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾. So the Sunnah, although it is not sent down [as revelation in the same way], is like what is sent down by virtue of that verse. Al-Hasan said concerning this verse: O son of Adam, you have been commanded to follow the Qur'an. There is no verse except that it is incumbent upon you to know concerning what it was revealed and what is meant by it, so that you may follow it and act upon it.

﴿And do not follow other than Him as protectors﴾. He means: whoever opposes the truth and contradicts it, do not follow him. He said ﴿other than Him as protectors﴾ because whoever adopts a school of thought, everyone who takes its path and follows it becomes one of its protectors. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And do not follow other than Him as protectors﴾. Malik ibn Dinar said: "And do not seek," meaning: seek. The meaning is: and do not seek other than Him as protectors. ﴿Little is it that you remember﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited: "yatadhakkarun" (they remember), and both readings have one meaning, namely: little is it that you take admonition.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 4:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And how many a town We have destroyed﴾. "Kam" (how many) is for abundance, and "rubba" (many a) is for fewness.

The poet said:

(How many a paternal aunt and maternal aunt of yours, O Jarir, [have I milked] ... so that the milk of the she-camels has been drawn for them.) This was said by al-Farazdaq.

﴿Then Our punishment came upon it by night﴾, meaning: Our punishment, by night, ﴿or they were taking a midday rest﴾. Its implied sense is: by night while they were sleeping, or by day while they were resting at midday, from al-qaylula (the midday rest).

Al-Zajjaj said: "Or they were taking a midday rest" means: or for the variation of the punishment, that is, once at night and once during the day, as we have explained. If someone says: He has said, ﴿And how many a town We have destroyed﴾, so what is the meaning of His words, ﴿Then Our punishment came upon it﴾, and how can the coming of the punishment be after the destruction? It is said: the meaning of His words, ﴿We have destroyed﴾, is that We decreed its destruction; then Our punishment came upon it. It is also said: His words, ﴿Then Our punishment came upon it﴾, are an explanation of His words, ﴿We have destroyed﴾, and His words, ﴿We have destroyed﴾, are His words, ﴿Then Our punishment came upon it﴾. This is like the saying of the speaker: "You gave me and so you were good to me"; there is no difference between it and his saying: "You were good to me in what you gave me," and each of the two is an explanation of the other. Likewise is this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 5:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So their plea was not but that they said, "Indeed, we were wrong-doers."﴾ "Their plea" (da'wahum) means their supplication (du'a'uhum). Sibawayh said: one says, "O Allah, make me among the da'wa (plea/supplication) of the Muslims," meaning among the supplication of the Muslims. So His words, ﴿So their plea was not but that they said, "Indeed, we were wrong-doers." when Our punishment came upon them⦆, mean: they were unable to repel the punishment when the punishment came upon them, and the final outcome of their affair was that they acknowledged their wrongdoing at a time when acknowledgment no longer benefits.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent﴾. This is a question of reproach, not a question of seeking information. That is, We will ask them about what they did regarding what reached them. ﴿And We will surely question the messengers﴾ about the conveying.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 7:

﴿So We will surely relate to them with knowledge﴾. That is: We will inform them of what they did, with insight and knowledge.

﴿And We were not absent﴾. For He, mighty and exalted, is with every individual through His knowledge and power.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the weighing on that Day is the truth﴾. Mujahid said: its meaning is: the judgment on that Day is with truth and justice. Most of the exegetes, however, hold that He meant by it the weighing with the well-known scale, and it is true. But how is it weighed? They differed. Some of them said: the records of deeds are weighed. It was also said: the persons themselves are weighed, and this is indicated by the saying of ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, who said: "A man, great and tall, who eats and drinks much, will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be weighed, yet he will not weigh the wing of a gnat in the sight of Allah." This has also been transmitted as a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) report.

It was also said: the deeds are weighed, for good deeds come in a good form and bad deeds come in an ugly form, and it is these that are weighed. And in a report it is said: "That scale has two pans, each pan as wide as the distance between the east and the west," and the scale is one for all, though it was also said that each person has a scale of his own. ﴿Then as for him whose scales are heavy, those are the successful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 9:

﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost their souls﴾, i.e., they cheated themselves ﴿because they used to wrong Our signs﴾. Al-Hasan said: "The scale of the one whose scale grows heavy is only heavy because of following the truth, and it is right that a scale in which the truth is placed should be heavy. And the scale of the one whose scale is light is only light because of following falsehood, and it is right that a scale in which nothing but falsehood is placed should be light."

It is narrated from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "The Messenger of Allah was sleeping one day with his head in my lap, and I wept, and my tears fell onto his cheek. The Messenger of Allah woke up and said: 'What is the matter with you?' I said: 'I remembered the Resurrection and its terrors. Will anyone remember anyone else on that day?' He said: 'As for three situations, no: at the scale, until it is known whether one's scale will be heavy or light; and at the flying of the pages, until it is known whether one's record will be placed in his right hand or [in] his left; and at the Sirat (bridge).'"

The saying of Allah, the Most High: ﴿And We have certainly established you upon the earth﴾. Tamkin (establishing, giving firm standing) here means tamlik (granting possession). ﴿And We made for you therein means of livelihood﴾, that is, causes by which you live. It is also said: We made for you that by which you reach livelihood. ﴿Little are you grateful.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 11:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We created you, then We fashioned you﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "We created you in the loins of Adam, then We fashioned you in the wombs of your mothers." Mujahid said: "We created you in the back of Adam, then We fashioned you on the Day of the Covenant (yawm al-mithaq), when He brought them forth like specks (kalladhdharr)." It was also said: this refers to Adam, peace be upon him, meaning: We created your origin, Adam, then We fashioned him. He mentioned it in the plural form while intending the singular. Al-Akhfash, who is one of the two opinions of Qutrub, said: "Thumma (then) here has the meaning of waw (and), i.e., and We fashioned you."

﴿Then We said to the angels: Prostrate yourselves to Adam﴾. If someone says: the command to the angels to prostrate was before the creation of the children of Adam, so what is the meaning of His saying ﴿Then We said to the angels﴾ following the mention of creation and fashioning?

The answer: As for the view of Mujahid, and the view of those who directed it to Adam, the statement is coherent.

As for the view of Ibn 'Abbas, this difficulty arises, and the answer to it is from several aspects:

The first: that what is meant is: "Then I inform you that We said to the angels: Prostrate yourselves to Adam." It was also said regarding it that there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its meaning is: "And We created you, then We said to the angels: Prostrate yourselves, then We fashioned you." It was also said that thumma has the meaning of waw, i.e., "And We said to the angels: Prostrate yourselves," and waw does not require sequence; this is the view of al-Akhfash and one of the two opinions of Qutrub. But they did not accept this from them, for the word thumma is not used with the meaning of waw, rather it indicates sequence (ta'qib).

﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis; he was not among those who prostrated﴾. We have already mentioned the prostration of the angels in Surat al-Baqarah, and that their prostration was to Adam.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?"﴾ The "lā" here is superfluous (zā'idah), and the meaning is: "What prevented you from prostrating?" Similar instances of this have already been mentioned.

﴿He said: "I am better than him. You created me from fire and You created him from clay."﴾ If it is said: Was this not an answer to what he was asked? It is said: Its implied sense is: he said, "I did not prostrate because I am better than him." It is also said that the question is implied within it, as if he were asked: "Are you better, or is he?" So he said: "I am better than him."

Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: The wicked one supposed, and considered that fire is better than clay, and did not know that excellence belongs to whomever God makes excellent, and God has preferred clay over fire. Moreover, in the nature of fire there is haste, lightness, and burning, whereas in clay there is steadiness, forbearance, humility, and trustworthiness, so it is permissible that it be better than fire. Ibn 'Abbas has said: "The first to exercise qiyas (analogical reasoning) was Iblis," as we have explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 13:

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Get you down from it﴾. That is: go out from it. The scholars differed concerning this pronoun (al-kinayah). It was said: He intended by it: descend from the Garden (al-Jannah). It was said: He intended by it: from the rank (al-darajah) in which God had placed you before. It was said: He intended by it: from the earth. For when God, exalted is He, expelled him, He removed him from the earth to the islands of the sea, and previously he had been the ruler (malik) of the earth, to the extent that it was said that he would not enter the earth except in fear, stealthily, in the form of an old man wearing tattered garments. ﴿It is not for you to be arrogant therein﴾, meaning: by abandoning prostration. ﴿So go out, for you are among the debased﴾, that is: the humiliated.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 14:

﴿He said, "Give me respite"﴾ meaning: grant me a reprieve ﴿until the Day they are resurrected﴾. He asked for a respite until the Resurrection.

Allah granted him respite in His words, ﴿He said, "Indeed, you are among those given respite."﴾ This respite was until the first blast of the Trumpet, as He said elsewhere in a restricted form: ﴿until the day of the appointed time﴾, and by it He meant the first blast.

If it is said: Is it permissible for Allah to answer the prayer of a disbeliever, since He answered the prayer of the accursed one (Iblis)? It is said: It is permissible by way of istidraj (gradual lead-on, the gradual drawing of a person toward punishment), trickery (makr) and respite (imla'), but not by way of honour (karamah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 16:

﴿He said, "Because You have led me astray"﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Bima aghwaytani" means "because You have caused me to go astray." It has also been said: "because You have frustrated me." So al-ighwa' (misguidance, leading astray) carries the meaning of al-khayba (frustration, failure). The poet said:

(Whoever meets with good, people praise his affair... and whoever goes astray will not lack someone blaming him for his error.)

That is: whoever fails will not lack someone blaming him for his failure. It has also been said that its meaning is: "Because You have called me to that by which You led me astray," ﴿Surely I will sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾, that is, on Your straight path, and it is the path of religion.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 17:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them﴾

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Mansur, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, that he said: ﴿I will surely come to them from before them﴾ means: from the direction of this world, by adorning it in their hearts so that they are deceived by it. ﴿And from behind them﴾ means: from the direction of the Hereafter, by saying: there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Fire. ﴿And from their right﴾ means: from the direction of good deeds. ﴿And from their left﴾ means: from the direction of evil deeds.

Ibn Abbas said, in the narration of al-Walibi from him: ﴿I will surely come to them from before them﴾ means: from the direction of the Hereafter, and ﴿from behind them﴾ means (i.e.) from the direction of this world. ﴿And from their right﴾: he obscures for them the matters of this world. ﴿And from their left﴾: he makes committing sins appealing to them.

Mujahid said: He intended by it: "I will come to them from all sides."

Qatadah said: The Wicked One did not say "from above them," because mercy descends upon them from above.

﴿And You will not find most of them grateful﴾ means: believers. If it is asked: how did the Wicked One know that he would not find most of them grateful? It is answered: he read it from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). It is also said: he said that as a guess, and so he was answered by the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And Iblis certainly confirmed his assumption about them﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Get out of it, disgraced and expelled.﴾ Al-A'mash recited "مذموما" (madhmuman, "blamed"), but the well-known reading is "مذءوما" (madhu'uman). Madhu'uman comes from al-dha'm (الذأم), which means fault or defect. It was also said that its meaning is "مقيتا" (maqitan, "detested"), from al-maqt (المقت, abhorrence).

﴿Expelled⁠⁠⁠⁠ (madhhuran)﴾: that is, banished. ﴿Whoever follows you among them, I will surely fill Hell with you all.﴾ The lam in "لأملان" (la-amla'anna) is the lam of oath, meaning: He swore that He would surely fill Hell with you all, from those who follow you among them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in the Garden﴾. This has already been explained. ﴿So eat from wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree, or you will be among the wrongdoers﴾. This has already been explained according to the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, that it was the tree of the sunbula (spikenard/ear of grain). It was also said: it was the fig tree. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: it was the camphor tree. It was also said: it was a tree from which the angels eat, called the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then Satan whispered to them both﴾. Waswasah (whispering) is a speech that Satan casts into the heart of a human being. The scholars differed over how he whispered to them while they were in the Garden and he was on the earth.

It was said: He whispered to them from the earth, because Allah, exalted is He, gave him a power by which he whispered to them, with that power, from the earth to the Garden. It was also said: when he whispered to them he was in the sky; so he and Adam met at the gate of the Garden, and he whispered. It was also said: the serpent concealed him in [its fangs] and brought him into the Garden, and he whispered from between [its fangs]; then the serpent was cursed and expelled from the Garden.

﴿That it might reveal to them what was concealed from them of their private parts﴾. The lam here is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), for he did not whisper for this purpose; rather, the outcome of their affair following his whispering was that he revealed to them what had been hidden of their nakedness.

﴿And he said, "Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree, lest you become two angels or become among the eternal."﴾ This was his whispering. Yahya ibn Abi Kathir and al-Dahhak recited ﴿malakayn﴾ with a kasrah on the lam, whereas the well-known reading is ﴿malakayn﴾ with a fathah on the lam. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala said: there was no kingship in the Garden belonging to other than Allah, so that one would say "malakayn" from "al-mulk" (kingship); rather, there were angels in it. Its meaning is: Allah forbade you to eat from this tree only because, if you eat from it, you would become two angels or become among the eternal.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 21:

﴿And he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers."﴾ He whispered to them and swore to it, and he was the first to swear by Allah falsely. So whoever swears by Allah falsely is among the followers of Iblis. And in a hadith: "Indeed, the believer can be deceived by Allah." When Iblis swore to what he whispered to them, Adam thought that no one swears by Allah except truthfully, out of the soundness of his heart, so he was deceived by him.

There is another view concerning it: that His saying, ﴿وقاسمهما﴾ (wa-qasamahuma, "and he swore to them"), derives from qismah (division, sharing), as if Iblis said to them: "Eat from this tree; whatever is good will be yours, and whatever is evil and harmful will be mine."

As for His saying, ﴿إِنِّي لَكمَا لمن الناصحين﴾ (innī lakumā laman al-nāṣiḥīn, "Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers"), it means: the guiding ones, those who wish good.

If someone says: His saying, ﴿مَا نهاكما رَبكُمَا عَن هَذِه الشَّجَرَة إِلَّا أَن تَكُونَا ملكَيْنِ﴾ (ma nahākumā rabbukumā ʿan hadhihi al-shajarati illā an takūnā malakayn, "Your Lord has forbidden you from this tree only lest you become two angels"), is evidence that the angels are superior to the children of Adam. It is said: its meaning, and Allah knows best, is that they saw the angels in the best form and the highest station, and in continuous glorification without fatigue or desire. So they wished to reach that station if they ate from that tree, and to be freed from fatigue and from human desire. There is no evidence in this that the angel is superior to the human being.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 22:

And His saying, ﴿So he led them on by deception﴾, meaning: He brought them down from the station of obedience to the state of disobedience. The poet said:

(And Joseph, when the children of ʿIlla lowered him down, ended up at the bottom of the well, dwelling there.)

As for al-ghurur (deception), it is showing sincere counsel while concealing deceit.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when they tasted the tree, their shameful parts became apparent to them﴾. In this there is evidence that they had not yet enjoyed the eating [fully]. Ibn ʿAbbas said: It was said that when they tasted it, punishment seized them, and their punishment was that their clothing fell away from them and their private parts became exposed.

﴿And they began to cover themselves with leaves from the Garden﴾. Thaʿlab said: They began to stick some leaves onto others and cover their nakedness with them. It is said: khasafa al-naʿl (he mended the sandal), when he placed one layer upon another. The scholars differed concerning those leaves. Ibn ʿAbbas, and most of the exegetes with him, said: They were the leaves of the fig and the olive. It was also said: they were banana leaves.

﴿And their Lord called out to them: Did I not forbid you from that tree, and tell you that Satan is a manifest enemy to you?﴾ That is: from eating of it. ﴿Manifest﴾ means: clearly hostile. It is related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and also reported from ʿAta', that they both said: When their shameful parts became apparent to them in the Garden, Adam fled through the Garden, and a tree caught hold of his hair. His Lord called to him: "Are you fleeing from Me, O Adam?" He said: "No, rather out of shame before You, O Lord."

The Lord, exalted is He, said: ﴿They said: "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾ Adam acknowledged the sin and asked for forgiveness. This is the difference between his disobedience and the disobedience of Iblis: Iblis disobeyed and persisted in disobedience, whereas Adam disobeyed and repented of the disobedience. Also, Iblis acted deliberately, whereas Adam acted in forgetfulness. The scholars differed over whether Adam knew, at the time of eating, that it was an act of disobedience. Some of them said: he knew it, but Allah forgave him and accepted his repentance. It was also said: a doubt entered him from the whispering of Iblis, and he was not acting deliberately, since he was infallible (ma'sum) as a prophet (nabi).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 24:

The words of God, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "Go down, some of you being enemies to others."﴾ If someone says: Had He not already addressed Iblis with the command to descend (al-hubut) before? What is the meaning of this repetition? It is said: this second address is to Adam, Eve and the serpent, as Abu Salih reported, and Iblis is excluded from the address. It is also said: the address is to all of them, because although they committed the sin at the time of the expulsion and the sending down, when they were gathered in the sending down, He combined them in the address. The first address was specific to Iblis, and the second address is general to all of them.

﴿And for you on the earth there is a dwelling place and provision for a time.﴾ In the stories (al-qasas) it is related that Adam fell in the land of India, Eve in Jeddah, the serpent in Maysan, and Iblis in Ayla. It is also said: in Madad. And it is said: Iblis fell in the land of Basra, then went out to the land of Egypt, and laid eggs and hatched his brood there.

It is related from Ibn Umar that he said: When God, exalted is He, expelled Iblis to the earth, he said: "O Lord, where is my dwelling?" He said: "The bathhouses." He said: "Where is my assembly?" He said: "The markets." He said: "And what is my food?" He said: "Every food over which the name of God has not been mentioned." He said: "And what is my drink?" He said: "Every intoxicant." He said: "And what is my snare?" He said: "Women." He said: "And what is my writing?" He said: "Tattooing." He said: "And who are my messengers?" He said: "The soothsayers."

God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿He said: "Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be brought forth."﴾ He means: the earth is where your life and your death are, and from it is your resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts﴾. If someone says: How does He say "We have sent down," when clothing does not descend from the sky? It is said: Rain has been sent down, and every plant comes from rain; so it is as if He sent it down. It is also said: the meaning is that everything on the earth is from the blessings of the sky, so it is like something sent down from the sky. On this basis is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We sent down iron, in which is great might﴾, whereas iron is extracted from the earth, but He attributed it to the sky. So too is this.

The occasion of revelation of the verse: in the Jahiliyyah they used to circumambulate the House naked, saying, "We will not circumambulate in garments in which we have disobeyed God, may He be exalted." Men circumambulated naked by day and women by night. So the verse was revealed prohibiting that. Al-Zuhri said: The Arabs used to circumambulate in this way, naked, except the Hums, who are the Quraysh and the allies of the Quraysh; they circumambulated in their clothing. They were called Hums because of their strictness in their religion, and from the same root is "al-hamasah" (valour) because of its severity. Mujahid said: The women used to circumambulate wearing a rahat, and the rahat is a piece of wool that does not fully conceal the private part, and sometimes it was of leather thong. Qatadah said: A woman among them would circumambulate placing her hand over her private part to conceal her nakedness with it, and say:

(Today some or all of it appears, and what appears of it, I do not make lawful.)

So His saying: ﴿We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts﴾ means: We have sent down to you that with which you cover your nakedness; so do not circumambulate the House naked. His saying: ﴿and as adornment (rishan)﴾. It was also read as "wa-riyashan" (and as plumage/adornment). Some distinguished between the two.

Mujahid said: al-Rish is wealth. Al-Kisa'i said: al-Rish is clothing.

As for al-Riyash: it is said it is livelihood; it is said "tarayyasha fulan" when a man finds what he lives on. It is also said: al-Riyash is the furnishings of the house. Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-Rish and al-Riyash are one and the same, and it is what appears of clothing and the adornment. Sibawayh recited:

(My plumage from you, and my love for you, though your visits are rare.)

That is, few. His saying: ﴿and the garment of piety﴾ is read in the accusative (meaning: and We have sent down to you the garment of piety), and it is read "wa-libasu al-taqwa" in the nominative, meaning: it is the garment of piety.

﴿Let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping them of their clothing to show them their private parts﴾.

Al-Qutaybi said: That is, the garment of piety is the clothing; for whoever fears God circumambulates clothed, not naked. In a hadith: "Indeed the garment of piety is modesty (haya')," because it impels one to piety; this is the saying of al-Hasan.

The poet said:

(Indeed, it is as if I see one who has no modesty and no trustworthiness among people, naked.)

Ikrimah said: Modesty and faith are in one bond; when one departs, the other follows it. Qatadah said: the garment of piety is faith. Uthman ibn Affan said: the garment of piety is good bearing. Urwah said: it is the fear of God. It is also said: the garment of piety here is the wool garment and the rough garment worn by people of scrupulousness. It is also said: it is righteous deeds.

﴿That is better﴾. It is said: "dhalika" is an expression of a trick, and its implied meaning is: and the garment of piety is better; so al-A'mash read it. It is also said: "dhalika" is in its place, and its meaning is: that which was mentioned of clothing and adornment, and everything mentioned is good. ﴿That is among the signs of God, that perhaps they may remember﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 27:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden﴾, meaning: let not Satan lead you astray, just as he tempted your parents and removed them from the Garden.

﴿He strips them of their clothing to show them their private parts﴾. This is what we mentioned concerning the falling away of their clothing when they ate from the tree. In it is evidence that they had not seen their nakedness before, since He said: "to show them their private parts." The scholars differed concerning what that clothing was. Ibn 'Abbas said: their clothing was of nails (dhufr), as if God, exalted is He, had clothed them in a material of the same kind as their nails. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: it was a garment of light.

﴿Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them﴾, meaning: and his soldiers (junud). The meaning is that Satan and his soldiers see you while you do not see them. ﴿Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe﴾, meaning: the devils take the disbelievers as their allies. This is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with strong incitement﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when they commit an indecency﴾. It has been said that the indecency here is their circumambulating the House naked. It has also been said that it is shirk (associating partners with Allah).

﴿They say: "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it."﴾ Say (O Muhammad): ﴿Indeed, Allah does not command indecency﴾, and indecency (fahsha') is every ugly act that has reached the utmost limit of ugliness. ﴿Do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice⁠﴾, that is: with equity and truthfulness. ﴿And set your faces upright at every place of prostration⁠﴾. On this there are three opinions. The first is that its meaning is: establish the prayer in every mosque in which prayer reaches you, and do not say, "We will delay it until we reach our mosque." The second is that its meaning is: face the qibla with your faces in every prayer. The third is that its meaning is: make your prayer and your worship sincere for God, may He be exalted.

﴿And call upon Him, making the religion sincerely His, as He originated you, you will return⁠﴾. That is: you will return alone, without family and without wealth, just as He created you alone, without family and without wealth. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time⁠﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is that your resurrection alive is like your creation at the beginning; both are easy for Him. The correct view, however, is that what is intended is that, just as He created you wretched and happy, and believers and disbelievers, so you will return in that same way; and this is what is indicated by

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A group He guided, and a group upon whom misguidance was made due﴾. That is: a group whom Allah guided, and a group whom Allah misguided; so misguidance became due for them. The hadith has been authenticated from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The truthful one, the one whose truthfulness is confirmed, told me – meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) – that a man may act with the deeds of the people of Paradise until there is between him and Paradise only a cubit's length, and then the Decree overtakes him, so he acts with the deeds of the people of the Fire and enters the Fire. And a man may act with the deeds of the people of the Fire until there is between him and the Fire only a cubit's length, and then the Decree overtakes him, so he acts with the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters Paradise."

﴿Indeed, they took the devils as protectors besides Allah, and they think that they are guided﴾. In this there is evidence that the one who is deluded into disbelief, who thinks he is upon the truth, is the same as the obstinate one.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 31:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer﴾ refers to the command to perform the circumambulation (tawaf) and the prayer while clothed. In the odd (shadhdh) interpretations (tafsir), it is said that it means combing the hair and wearing sandals. It is also said that He intended by it tranquility (sakinah) and dignity (waqar), and this is the meaning of what is related from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "When you come to the prayer, do not come to it running, but come to it walking, and upon you is tranquility and dignity."

﴿And eat and drink﴾. Al-Farra' said: He only commanded them to eat and drink because in the Jahiliyyah they used to abstain from eating meat and fat during the season of pilgrimage, just as they abstained from clothing during the circumambulation, and they would say: "We abstain from meat and fat for the sake of Allah, exalted is He."

﴿And do not be excessive﴾, i.e., by making lawful what Allah has made unlawful, and by making unlawful what Allah has made lawful, and every wealth spent in disobedience to Allah is excess (israf). The root meaning of israf is going beyond the limit, either by extremism or by negligence. ﴿Indeed, He does not love the excessive﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants?﴾ He means: the clothing during the circumambulation (tawaf). ﴿And the good things of provision?﴾ He means: what they forbade for themselves of eating meat during the days of the season (mawsim), along with all that they forbade of the bahira, the sa'iba and the like. ﴿Say: They are for those who believed in the life of this world, purely [for them] on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ Most of the exegetes said, and this is the view of al-Dahhak: there is an ellipsis (hadhf) in it, and its estimated meaning is: they are for those who believed and for the polytheists in the life of this world, purely for the believers on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: its meaning is: purely from disturbance and grief on the Day of Resurrection, for they have them in this world together with disturbance and grief. ﴿Thus do We detail the signs for a people who know.﴾

"The Word of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say, 'My Lord has only forbidden the indecent acts, what is apparent of them and what is concealed'﴾. Qatadah said: They are fornication, secretly and openly. Others said: What is apparent of them is marrying within the forbidden degrees (nikah al-mahārim), and what is concealed is fornication. ﴿And sin and oppression without right﴾. As for al-ithm (sin), there are three opinions:

The first: al-Farra' said: everything that falls short of the prescribed legal punishment (hadd). It was also said: it is all acts of disobedience. And it was said: al-ithm is wine, and this usage is attested in poetry:

(I drank al-ithm until my intellect went astray... Thus al-ithm takes away the minds.)

As for al-baghy (oppression), it was said: it is arrogance over people. And it was said: it is corruption. Tha'lab said: it is that one attacks people without right. ﴿And that you associate with Allah﴾, and its implied meaning is: and He has forbidden that you associate partners with Allah ﴿for which He has sent down no authority﴾, i.e., no proof, ﴿and that you say about Allah what you do not know﴾, because they used to attribute all the indecent acts and polytheism they committed to Allah, the Exalted, saying: 'We do it by the command of Allah.' So this is their saying about Allah what they do not know."

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And for every nation there is a term﴾, meaning: the span of life. ﴿So when their term comes, they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾

If it is said: Why did He single out the hour, saying they cannot delay it by an hour, rather than [saying they cannot delay or advance it] by anything else? It is said: He singled it out only because it is the smallest of the known measures of time."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 35:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O Children of Adam, if there come to you⦅messengers⦆ from among you...﴾. His words "imma" (إِمَّا) are two words: "in" (إِن) and "ma" (مَا), and one of them has been assimilated into the other. Its meaning is: "when there comes to you," and "if there comes to you." ﴿Messengers from among you﴾: it has been said that by this he meant only our Messenger (ﷺ), and it has been said that he meant all the messengers. ﴿Who recite My verses to you, then whoever fears Allah and makes amends﴾: that is, fears shirk (associating partners with Allah), and sets right what is between himself and his Lord. ﴿Then there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who denied Our signs and waxed arrogant against them﴾. He mentioned the arrogance because every denier and every disbeliever is arrogant, and they only denied and disbelieved out of arrogance. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," they were arrogant﴾, meaning they were arrogant about acknowledging His oneness. ﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs?﴾ We have already explained this invention (ifti'a'). ﴿Those will receive their portion of what is decreed in the Book.﴾ Concerning this there are five opinions:

The first, which is the view of Ibn 'Abbas: it means what has been decreed for them of good and evil.

The second, the view of Mujahid: it means what they were promised of good and evil.

The third, the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr: it means what has been decreed for them of misery and happiness.

The fourth, the view of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: he meant by it the term of life (ajal), the deeds, and the provision.

There is also a fifth, well-known opinion: it means their portion of the punishment mentioned in the Book, for the Book mentions the punishment of the disbelieving groups, such as the hypocrites, the Jews, the Christians, and the polytheists.

﴿Until, when Our messengers come to them to take them in death,⦆ i.e., the Angel of Death and his helpers, ﴿to take them in death⦆, i.e., to take the full number of their terms. ﴿They will say, "Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?"⦆ i.e., the messengers say to the disbelievers: Where are those whom you used to invoke besides Allah, the idols? ﴿They will say, "They have vanished from us,"⦆ i.e., they have gone away and disappeared from us, ﴿and they will testify against themselves that they had been disbelievers.⦆

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 38:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Enter among nations﴾, meaning: together with nations, and this is like the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

(And can one who was near to his era of thirty months ... be made to rejoice in three states?)

That is: together with three states. It was also said: its meaning is: enter amid nations (﴿qad khalat﴾), that is, who have passed away, ﴿before you, of jinn and humankind, into the Fire﴾. In this there is evidence that the jinn die as humankind do, contrary to the saying of al-Hasan, when he said: they do not die.

﴿Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister﴾. Al-Farra' said: meaning, its sister in religion, not in lineage; that is, the Jews curse the Jews, and the Christians the Christians.

﴿Until, when they have all overtaken one another therein﴾, that is: they caught up with one another, followed one another in succession, and gathered therein, ﴿all together, the last of them will say of the first of them﴾. By this is meant: the last of each nation and the first of each nation. It was also said: it means the last of them to enter and the first of them to enter, namely the leaders together with the followers, for the leaders enter first.

﴿Our Lord, these led us astray﴾, meaning: the leaders led us astray. ﴿So give them a double punishment from the Fire﴾, that is: multiply the punishment for them. ﴿He will say: for each is double, but you do not know﴾. Read with the ta' (you, plural), his words ﴿but you do not know﴾ mean: O people, you do not know. As for one who reads it with the ya' (they), its meaning is: the leaders do not know what is due to the followers, nor do the followers know what is due to the leaders.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the first of them will say to the last of them﴾, meaning: the leaders, to ﴿the last of them﴾, meaning: the followers, ﴿So you had no superiority over us﴾. Al-Suddi said: its meaning is that you disbelieved as we disbelieved, and you denied as we denied, so you have no superiority over us. And it was said: its meaning is: you had no superiority over us in lightening the punishment. ﴿So taste the punishment for what you used to earn.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them - the gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾. Know that the gates of heaven are opened for three things: for deeds, for supplications, and for souls. And in the report: "The angel ascends with the soul of the believer, and it has a pleasant scent, so the gates of heaven are opened for it. And he ascends with the soul of the disbeliever, and it has a foul stench, so the gates of heaven are closed to it, and he is ordered to cast it into the sijjin. This is His saying, exalted is He: (﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn. Nay, indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn﴾)." The meaning of the verse is: the gates of heaven will not be opened for the deeds, supplications, or souls of the disbelievers.

(﴿41﴾) ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds - We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity - those are the companions of Paradise﴾.

It is also said: its meaning is, the gates of Paradise will not be opened for them, but it was expressed by "the gates of heaven," because the gates of Paradise are in heaven.

﴿And they will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas read: "yalij al-jamal" with a raised jim and a shaddah on the mim. Saʿid ibn Jubayr read: "ḥattā yalij al-jamal" with a raised jim and a light mim. Ibn Sirin read: "fī sum al-khiyāṭ" with a raised sin. The well-known reading is ﴿ḥattā yalij al-jamal fī sum al-khiyāṭ﴾, and this is the well-known camel. Ibn Masʿud was asked about this camel and said: "It is the mate of the she-camel," as if he considered the questioner foolish for asking about what is not hidden. It is related from al-Hasan that he said: "It is the thick rope upon which are two black cables." As for the camel that Ibn Masʿud recited, it is the cable (qalas) of the ship. As for "al-jumal" with a light mim, it is said to be also the cable of the ship, and it is said to be the rope of the ship. As for "al-summ" and "al-sum," they are the same, and it is the hole of the needle. The purpose of the verse is to emphasise the prohibition of their entering Paradise, and this is common in the speech of the Arabs. It is like their saying: "I will not do such and such until the raven turns white," and "until the pitch turns white." The poet said:

(When the raven turns grey, I come to my family... and the pitch becomes like milk, fresh)

The qar and the qir: a black substance, used as a proverbial comparison; it is said: "something like pitch and tar in blackness." ﴿And thus do We recompense the criminals﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will have a bed of Hell beneath them, and above them coverings.﴾ That is, a spread (*mihad*). ﴿And above them coverings﴾ means blankets (*luhaf*). This is like His saying: ﴿They will have above them canopies of fire, and beneath them canopies.﴾

Sibawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The tanwin (nunation) in His saying ﴿ghawashin﴾ is not original (*ghayr asliyy*). Rather, it is a substitute (*badal*) for the yā' (ي), and its origin is *ghawashī*. Similar examples are many (﴿And thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾
And those who believed and did righteous deeds (We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity), i.e., its capacity. ﴿Those are the companions of the Garden; they will abide therein forever.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 43:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts; beneath them rivers will flow﴾. Al-ghill (resentment) is deceit and malice. It is related from ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "I hope that I, ʿUthman, Talha and al-Zubayr are among those of whom Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾."

Muslim related in his Sahih, with his chain of narration, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "When the believers are delivered from the Sirat, they will be held back at a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, and some of them will take retribution from others. When they have been cleansed and purified, they will be given permission to enter Paradise. By Him in whose hand my soul is, one of them will be more guided to his dwelling in Paradise than he was to his dwelling in this world." And in some reports: "At the gate of Paradise there is a spring from which the people of Paradise drink and bathe, and thereby resentment and malice are removed from their hearts; then they enter Paradise."

﴿And they will say: "Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this. We would never have been guided had Allah not guided us."﴾ In this there is evidence against the Qadariyya. ﴿Certainly the messengers of our Lord came with the truth, and they will be called out: "This is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do."﴾ Tilka (that) is the feminine form of dhalika (that). The meaning of the verse is: as though, when they see Paradise from afar, they are called out: "That is Paradise." It is also said: this calling will occur within Paradise, and they will be told: "This is the Paradise which you have inherited." In a report: "Every one of you has a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. The believer inherits from the disbeliever his dwelling in Paradise, and the disbeliever inherits from the believer his dwelling in the Fire."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised to be true?"﴾ This takes place before they are sent to Jahannam. ﴿They will say: "Yes."﴾ We have already explained that the answer to a question that contains negation (jahd) is "balā" (rather, yes), while the answer to a question that does not contain negation is "naʿam" (yes). ﴿Then a caller will proclaim between them: "The curse of God is upon the wrongdoers."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 7, verse 45:

﴿Those who turn away from the way of Allah﴾ meaning: they turn away from the religion. ﴿And seek to make it عوجا (crooked)﴾ meaning: they seek to make the religion deviant, and عوج here means الزيغ (deviation). ( ﴿And they are disbelievers in the Hereafter﴾

And between them is a barrier (ḥijāb). This is a barrier between Paradise and Hellfire. ﴿And upon the heights (al-A'rāf) are men﴾. It has been said: al-A'rāf is a wall between Paradise and Hellfire, as in His saying: ﴿So a wall with a gate will be struck between them﴾. It has also been said: it is an elevated place. The first view is more correct, and most scholars hold it.

As for the men who are upon al-A'rāf, the scholars differed concerning them. Ibn Mas'ūd, Ḥudhayfah, and ʿAṭā' said: they are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal. Abū Mijlaz Lāḥiq ibn Ḥumayd said: they are a people from among the angels in the form of men from mankind. Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, in his tafsir, related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "They are a people who fought (in battle) without the permission of their parents, so they were martyred, and they remain on al-A'rāf: their martyrdom prevents them from entering the Fire, and their disobedience to their parents prevents them from entering Paradise."

Al-Ḥasan said: they are people of merit among the believers, placed upon al-A'rāf, so they look out over the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, observing the conditions of both groups. ﴿They recognise each by their marks﴾, i.e., they recognise the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces, and the people of the Fire by the blackness of their faces.

﴿And they call out to the companions of Paradise: "Peace be upon you"﴾. So when they see the people of Paradise, they say: "Peace be upon you." ﴿They have not entered it﴾, meaning: the companions of al-A'rāf have not entered Paradise. ﴿Yet they hope﴾, meaning: to enter Paradise. Al-Ḥasan said: "He who placed hope in their hearts will bring them to what they hope for." Ḥudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Allah does not disappoint their hopes."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when their sights are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."﴾ He means: when they look upon the people of the Fire and what they are in, they seek refuge with Allah from the Fire.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the companions of the Heights will call out to men whom they recognize by their marks﴾. It has been said: they will see the disbelievers and recognize them, such as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Abu Jahl, Abu Lahab and their like, and they will call out to them. ﴿They will say: "Your massing together did not avail you, nor did what you used to be arrogant about"﴾. That is, your gathering and your mutual support did not benefit you in the world. ﴿And what you used to be arrogant about﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 49:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Is it these about whom you swore that Allah would not bestow His mercy upon them?﴾ This was when they said what they said to the disbelievers, and then they look toward the people of Paradise and see Khabbab, ʿAmmar, Bilal, Suhayb and others like them. The people of the A'raf (the heights between Paradise and Hell) then say to those disbelievers: ﴿Is it these about whom you swore that Allah would not bestow His mercy upon them?﴾ Meaning: "Are these the ones you swore would never enter Paradise, when they have entered it?" That is, Khabbab, ʿAmmar and the like.

Then Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Enter Paradise; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve.﴾

There is another opinion: that when the people of the A'raf say to those disbelievers what they say, the disbelievers reply to them: "If those people have entered Paradise while we are in the Fire, then you have not entered Paradise yet." So they taunt them over this and swear that they (will not enter) Paradise. Then Allah, exalted is He, says to those disbelievers: ﴿Is it these about whom you swore that Allah would not bestow His mercy upon them? Enter Paradise; no fear shall be upon you﴾, He says this to the people of the A'raf, and He admits them into Paradise, ﴿nor shall you grieve.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 50:

The Exalted said: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: "Pour upon us some water, or some of what Allah has provided you."﴾ In this is evidence that, just as they are tormented with the Fire, there will also be upon them the torment of hunger and thirst alongside the torment of the Fire, until they ask for food and drink.

And in a report: "A man from the people of the Fire sees his brother or companion in Paradise, and says to him from the Fire: 'O my brother, give me relief with a sip of water, for I have been burned.' He replies: 'Allah has forbidden it to the disbelievers.' This is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿They say, "Indeed, Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers."﴾ meaning: the food and the drink. This is a prohibition of prevention, not a prohibition of worship (taʿabbud). Know that giving water to drink carries a great reward. And in a report from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever gives a believer a sip of water, Allah will distance him from Hell by the length of a horse's course (shawt faras)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 51:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who took their religion as amusement and play, and whom the worldly life deceived﴾. Its meaning: eating and drinking. This was said by Abdullah ibn al-Harith. It was also said: its meaning is: those whose aspiration was the world and whose preoccupation was with it; they are the ones who took their religion as amusement and play, and the worldly life deceived them.

﴿So today We will forget them﴾, that is, We will leave them, ﴿as they forgot the meeting of this their day﴾, that is, as they left off working for the meeting of this their day, ﴿and as they were denying Our signs﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 52:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We had certainly brought them a Book﴾, meaning: We brought them the Qur'an. ﴿Which We have detailed﴾, meaning: We made clear what is in it of the lawful (ḥalāl) and the unlawful (ḥarām). ﴿With knowledge﴾, meaning: with knowledge of what would benefit them. It was also said: its meaning is with knowledge of the reward and the punishment. ﴿A guidance﴾, meaning: guiding. ﴿And a mercy﴾, meaning: possessing mercy. ﴿For a people who believe﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 53:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they await anything but its final outcome?﴾ That is: do they await anything but [the fulfilment of] its final outcome (ta'wil). Mujahid said: its meaning is "anything but its recompense." Qatadah said: "anything but its consequence." The real meaning is: they await nothing but what their affair will end up with, namely the destiny of the people of Paradise to Paradise, and the people of the Fire to the Fire. ﴿On the day its final outcome comes﴾ That is: its recompense and what their affair will come to.

﴿Those who had forgotten it will say﴾ That is: those who had abandoned it before. ﴿"The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth. So do we have any intercessors who might intercede for us, or could we be sent back [to the world] so that we might act differently from what we used to do?"﴾ ﴿They have lost their souls﴾ That is: they diminished the due of their own souls. ﴿And what they used to invent has forsaken them﴾ That is: it went away and was lost to them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 54:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾.

Mujahid said: [the six days] are from Sunday to Friday. If it is asked: how can He say "in six days" when there were no days at the time He created the heavens and the earth? It is said: what makes us know that they did not exist? Rather, they did exist, for Allah, may He be exalted, has informed us, and His word and His report are true. It is also said: it is permissible that what is meant is the measure of six days.

If it is asked: what is the wisdom in creating them in six days, when He was able to create them in the twinkling of an eye? It is said: creating them deliberately is more indicative of wisdom, so He created them deliberately so that it would be more indicative of His wisdom and the subtlety of His governance. In it there is also teaching for people and an admonition to the servants to be deliberate in affairs. And in a report: "Deliberation is from Allah, and haste is from Satan."

﴿Then He established Himself above the Throne﴾. The Mu'tazilah interpreted "istiwa'" (establishment) as "istila'" (taking control), and they recited of it:

(Bishr has established himself over Iraq, / without sword and without spilled blood.)

As for the People of the Sunnah, they disavow this interpretation and say: establishment above the Throne is an attribute of Allah, may He be exalted, "without how" (bi-la kayf), and belief in it is obligatory. Likewise it is related from Malik ibn Anas and other early scholars (al-salaf) that they said regarding this verse: belief in it is obligatory, and asking about it is an innovation (bid'ah).

﴿He covers the night over the day﴾, i.e., He makes the night cover the day. There is an ellipsis here, and its full sense is: He makes the night cover the day and makes the day cover the night, as He said in another verse: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night﴾ [39:5], ﴿seeking it urgently﴾, i.e., swiftly. This is because each of them follows the other and succeeds it in its track, as if it were in pursuit of it.

﴿And the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command﴾, i.e., made subservient to what He wills from them. ﴿Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, i.e., exalted in His oneness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾, meaning: humbly submitting, abjectly lowly, and reverent; and "secretly" means quietly. ﴿Indeed, He does not like transgressors﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: raising the voice in supplication is transgression. It is related in a report from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There will be people who transgress in purification and in supplication." And it is narrated that he saw some people shouting in supplication, so he said to them: "Lower your voices upon yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent; rather, you are calling upon One who is All-Hearing and near, and He is with you," meaning with knowledge and power. It was also said: among transgression in supplication is that one asks for himself a rank for which he is not fit, such as asking for the rank of the prophets when he is not a prophet, or the rank of the martyrs when he is not a martyr.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 56:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after it has been set in order﴾. That is: after the earth has been set in order by the religion (dīn) and the Sharia (sharī'ah, the sacred law). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: Among the corruption on the earth is diverting the water (taghwīr al-miyāh, making water sink deeper into the ground), cutting down fruit-bearing trees, and breaking dirhams and dinars.

﴿And call upon Him in fear and in hope﴾. That is: in fear of Allah and in hope of His reward. ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the good-doers.﴾ [Then the verse continues:] ﴿It is He who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, until when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land and send down water therefrom and bring forth from it all kinds of fruits. Thus do We bring forth the dead; perhaps you will remember.﴾ ... from the good-doers.

If it is asked: "qarīb" (near) is a masculine adjective, and "raḥmah" (mercy) is feminine, and Allah the Exalted said "qarīb" and did not say "qarībah." It is answered: al-Zajjāj said: "raḥmah" here means pardon and forgiveness; al-Akhfash said: it means bestowal of favour. Thus the adjective refers to the meaning rather than to the wording. Al-Farrā' said: when nearness is in terms of kinship, the adjective for a feminine noun takes the feminine form; but when nearness is not in terms of kinship, the adjective may be used in both masculine and feminine forms. They recited as evidence:

(At an evening when neither ʿAfrāʾ is near to you, so that she draws close, nor ʿAfrāʾ is far from you.)

Thus he used the adjective once in the feminine and once in the masculine.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 57:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings﴾ are read "bushran" (bushran), from al-bushara (good news). It is also read "nushran" (nushran), which is the plural of nashur (nashur), like rasul (messenger) and rusul (messengers). This refers to a pleasant wind. It is also read "nushran" with the shin vowelled with a sukun (nushran), which is likewise the plural of nashur, like rasul and rusul, and kitab (book) and kutub (books).

﴿Before His mercy﴾: meaning, the rain. ﴿Until, when they carry heavy clouds﴾: meaning, they lift up, that is, carry, ﴿heavy clouds﴾: meaning, laden with water. ﴿We drive them to a dead land, and We send down water thereby, and bring forth thereby fruits of every kind. Thus We bring forth the dead; perhaps you will remember﴾. He used the revival of the earth after its death as evidence for the revival of the dead, and in this there is clear proof. And in some reports: "Between the two blasts there will be forty years. Then Allah, the Exalted, will send down rain from the sky like the semen of men, and it will enter the earth, and people will grow from it. Then they will be resurrected with the second blast."

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And the good land - its vegetation comes out by the permission of its Lord﴾. ﴿But that which is bad﴾, meaning the salty land, ﴿does not yield except sparingly﴾, meaning: little and meagre. The poet said:

(So give what you have given, good; there is no good in the one who is scant and the one who is scant...)

This is a parable which Allah, the Exalted, has struck for the believers and the disbelievers. The believer brings forth what comes out of his soul of faith and good deeds easily and generously, while the disbeliever brings forth of good deeds only meagrely and little. ﴿Thus do We vary the signs for a people who give thanks﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day."﴾ In this verse He mentions the story of Noah and his people, and it will come (later in the commentary).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verses 60–61:

﴿The chiefs of his people said, "Indeed, we see you in evident error." He said, "O my people, there is no error in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."﴾

Allah, the Exalted, taught people good manners of speech through His saying: "There is no error in me," and He did not say, "You are in error," as is our habit (in such matters).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verses 60–61:

﴿The chiefs of his people said, "Indeed, we see you in evident error." He said, "O my people, there is no error in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds."﴾

Allah, the Exalted, taught people good manners of speech through His saying: "There is no error in me," and He did not say, "You are in error," as is our habit (in such matters).

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿I convey to you the messages of my Lord and I give you sincere counsel﴾. Naseeha (sincere counsel) is that one wishes for another the good that one wishes for oneself. Its meaning: I guide you, [showing] that I wish for myself what I wish for you. ﴿And I know from Allah what you do not know﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you, to warn you?﴾

*Al-'ajab* (wonder, astonishment) is a change that occurs in the soul upon seeing something whose inner reality is hidden from it. {so that you may be wary, and that you may receive mercy

So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ark (al-fulk). That is: in the ship.

﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs.﴾ The story will come (later). ﴿Indeed, they were a blind people.﴾ That is: blind to the truth.

"And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud." That is, "And We sent to 'Ad." Al-Farra' said: He was their brother by lineage, not in religion. And it was said: He meant by this that he was a human being like them. ﴿He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Will you not then fear Him?"﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 66:

﴿The chiefs among his people who disbelieved said: Indeed, we see you in foolishness.﴾ That is: in folly and ignorance. {And indeed, we think you are among the liars.}
He said: ﴿O my people, there is no folly in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.﴾ And this is also from good reply.
﴿I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am a sincere and trustworthy adviser to you.﴾ And we have already explained the meaning of naṣīḥ (sincere counsel).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 69:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you? And remember when He made you successors (khulafa') ﴾ — meaning: in the earth — ﴿after the people of Noah﴾, i.e., after their destruction.

(And He increased you in creation with broad stature.) By this He means: largeness of stature in height. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and al-Suddi said: the tallest of the people of 'Ad was one hundred cubits in height, and the shortest of them was sixty cubits in height. ﴿So remember the bounties of Allah that you may prosper.﴾

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They said, "Have you come to us so that we worship Allah alone and abandon what our fathers used to worship?"﴾ That is, the idols. ﴿So bring us what you threaten us with﴾ that is, the punishment. ﴿If you are among the truthful.﴾

"His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said: Punishment and wrath have already fallen upon you from your Lord.﴾ Rijs and rijz: it is the punishment. And ghadab (wrath): it is displeasure. ﴿Do you dispute with me about names﴾ that is: for the sake of names ﴿which you have named, you and your fathers﴾ that is, the idols, which you carved and named, you and your fathers. ﴿Allah has sent down no authority for them﴾ that is: no proof. ( ﴿So wait; I am with you among those who wait.﴾"

Then We saved him and those with him (Hud and his people) by a mercy from Us, and We cut off the root of those who denied Our signs and were not believers. That is, We cut off their origin and uprooted them with punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 73:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih﴾ means: And We sent to Thamud their brother Salih. ﴿He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah, as a sign for you."﴾ They asked him to bring forth from the rock a she-camel, and they pointed to a hard, smooth rock. So Salih, peace be upon him, supplicated, and the rock quaked as a pregnant woman quakes in labour, and the she-camel emerged; and she immediately gave birth to a young camel (saqab). ﴿So leave her to eat on Allah's earth.﴾ It was said: they had a valley from which they drank, so they made one day for the she-camel and one day for themselves; on her day the she-camel would drink all the water of the valley, and in exchange she would provide them with milk. ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest a painful punishment seize you.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad and settled you in the land﴾, meaning: He caused you to dwell (anzalakum) in it. The poet said:

(So he was settled in the midst of their people... and their settlement was completed among their folk)

﴿You take for yourselves palaces from its plains and hew out the mountains as houses﴾. They used to dwell in the summer in houses of mud, and in the winter they dwelt in houses they had hewn into the mountain. It was also said: they only hewed the houses in the mountain because houses of mud did not last for the duration of their lives, given how long their lives were. ﴿So remember the bounties of God﴾, meaning the blessings of God, ﴿and do not spread corruption in the land, causing mischief﴾. Al-'ayth (ʿayth): the most severe corruption.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The eminent ones among his people who were arrogant said to those who were deemed weak, to those of them who believed﴾. Meaning: the disbelievers among them said to the believers, ﴿Do you know that Salih is a messenger from his Lord?﴾ This is a question intended as a denial, because they used to deny his being sent. ﴿They said: Indeed we are believers in what he has been sent with.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verses 76–78:

The eminent ones among his people who were arrogant said to those who had been oppressed, to those among them who believed: "Do you know that Salih is sent from his Lord?" They said: "We are believers in that with which he has been sent." Those who were arrogant said: "Indeed we, in what you have believed in, are disbelievers." Then they hamstrung the she-camel and defied the command of their Lord. Al-'Utuw (defiance, transgression) is excess in falsehood. ﴿And they said: "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are indeed one of the messengers."﴾ That is: of the punishment. ﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾ Al-Rajfah: the quaking of the earth and its shaking. They had been destroyed by the Sayhah (blast) and the Rajfah. ﴿So they became, in their homes, prostrate corpses.﴾ That is: lifeless and dead. From this comes "al-ramad al-jathim" (the motionless ash). It was also said: "jathimin" means fallen on their knees and faces. It was also said: they were burned by a thunderbolt until they became like motionless ash.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verses 76–78:

The eminent ones among his people who were arrogant said to those who had been oppressed, to those among them who believed: "Do you know that Salih is sent from his Lord?" They said: "We are believers in that with which he has been sent." Those who were arrogant said: "Indeed we, in what you have believed in, are disbelievers."
