Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 79:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So he turned away from them and said: "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisors."﴾ If someone says: How did he address them when they had perished? It is said: This is like the Messenger (ﷺ) addressing the disbelievers slain on the day of Badr when he threw them into the qalib (well). He came to the edge of the well and said: "O Utbah, O Shaybah, and O Abu Jahl, I have found what my Lord promised me to be true; have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?" Then Umar said: "O Messenger of God, how do you address a people who have already begun to rot?" He said: "You are not more able to hear than they are, but they are unable to respond." It is also said: He addressed them with it so that it would be a lesson for those who came after them. It is also said: In the verse there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir, i.e. rearrangement of its order), and its intended sense is: So he turned away from them, then the quake seized them, and they became prostrate in their homes; and that is because God, exalted is He, would not punish a people while their prophet was among them.

Abu al-Zubayr narrated from Jabir: "The Prophet passed by the dwellings of Thamud in the lands of Tabuk, and he said to his companions: O people, do not ask God for signs, for these people asked for the she-camel, so God brought it out for them; it used to come to water from this mountain pass and depart from this mountain pass, but they slaughtered it, so God sent down the punishment upon them, and none of them escaped except a man who was in the sacred precinct (haram). When he came out, there befell him what had befallen the rest of them of the punishment. That man was called Abu Righal."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Lot, when he said to his people﴾. That is: We sent Lot, and mention Lot when he said to his people: ﴿Do you commit the abomination﴾. Al-fahisha (the abomination): the vile deed which is extremely repugnant. ﴿No one in the worlds has preceded you in it﴾. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn Abbas: that deed had not been committed by anyone before them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 81:

﴿Indeed, you approach men with desire, instead of women.﴾ He explains that "that abomination" ﴿Nay, you are a people who exceed the limits.﴾ That is: those who go beyond the bounds of what is commanded.

The words of Him, exalted be He: ﴿And the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel them from your town. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."﴾ Its meaning: they keep themselves clean of anal intercourse with men. Qatadah said: They blamed them without any valid blame, and found fault with them without any real fault.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 83:

The words of the Most High: ﴿So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind.﴾ That is, among those who remained (al-ghabirin) in the punishment. It is said: "ghabara" means "baqiya," to remain. And they recited the verse:

(And you are not, O Mu'add, among men... one who asks about this and that, what the news is)

(Rather, I am the one whose support is al-Asfar ibn Qays... for what has passed and what remains)

It is also said that its meaning is: among those who remained behind from salvation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 84:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We rained upon them a rain﴾. In the narrative, God, exalted is He, sent Jibril, upon him be blessings from God, until he uprooted their cities. It is said: they were cities which he uprooted, lifted up to the sky, and then overturned. For this reason they were called al-mu'tafikah (the overturned), because they were turned over and overthrown. As for the raining down with stones, it was upon those among them who strayed far (shadhdha) in the roads. It is also said: after He had overturned them, He rained stones down upon them, ﴿So look how was the end of the criminals﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to Madyan﴾, meaning: and We sent to Madyan. It was said: he is Madyan ibn Ibrahim al-Khalil (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and those people were of his progeny. It was also said: this is not so, rather it is the name of a tribe.

And His saying: ﴿their brother Shu'ayb﴾, meaning: in lineage, not in religion. ﴿He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord.﴾ If someone says: what is the meaning of His saying ﴿there has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord﴾, when they had no sign? It is said: rather they did have a sign, but it is not mentioned in the Qur'an, and not every sign is mentioned in the Qur'an. ﴿So give full measure and weight﴾, and they used to worship idols and cheat in the weights. ﴿And do not deprive people of their due things﴾, meaning: do not diminish their rights.

﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation﴾, meaning: after its reformation through the sending of the Messenger and the command to justice. ﴿That is better for you, if you are believers﴾, meaning: if you believe, that is better for you. It was also said: its meaning is: "if you were not believers."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not sit on every path, threatening and turning away from the way of Allah⁠﻿—﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿﻿...⁠ Let me give this properly:

Translation:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not sit on every path threatening⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠...⁠

Correction, the full translation follows:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do not sit on every path, threatening and turning away from the way of Allah who believes in Him, seeking to make it crooked.﴾ "Path" (ṣirāṭ) means a road (ṭarīq). The poet said:

(We beat their people with horses until We made them more humbled than the path)

He means: more humbled than the road.

﴿Threatening and turning away from the way of Allah﴾ It is said: they used to send men to the roads to threaten people. When a man wished to believe in Shu'ayb and went to him, they would threaten him and say: "If you believe in Shu'ayb, we will kill you." This is the meaning of His saying ﴿threatening⁠﻿﻿⁠﻿﻿...⁠

Translation (complete and corrected):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not sit on every path, threatening and turning away from the way of Allah.﴾ "Path" (ṣirāṭ) means a road (ṭarīq). The poet said:

(We beat their people with horses until We made them more humbled than the path)

He means: more humbled than the road.

﴿Threatening and turning away from the way of Allah⁠⁠⁠⁠...⁠

Almighty God's words: ﴿And if there is a group among you who have believed in that with which I have been sent, and a group who have not believed﴾. That is because some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. ﴿So be patient until God judges between us, and He is the best of judges﴾.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The chiefs of those among his people who were arrogant said: "We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believed with you, from our town, or you will return to our religion."﴾ It was said by the disbelievers of his people. ﴿He said: "Even if we were unwilling?"﴾ Meaning: "Would you do this even though we are unwilling?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 89:

﴿We have indeed fabricated a lie against Allah if we return to your religion after Allah has rescued us from it.﴾ If it is asked: how is the word "return" (al-'awd) correct when it is said of Shu'ayb, since he was never upon their religion at all? It is answered: its meaning is "if we become [adherents] of your religion," and 'āda (returned) here carries the sense of ṣāra (became) and kāna (was), as the poet said:

(If the days were once kinder to me... then sins have come to be for them.)

That is, "there were sins for them."

And His saying: ﴿after Allah has rescued us from it﴾ means: from entering their religion from the outset. It is also said that what is meant is the people of Shu'ayb. ﴿And it is not for us to return to it, except that Allah, our Lord, wills﴾. If it is asked: does Allah will their return to disbelief? It is answered: what prevents that? The verse accords with the view of the People of the Sunnah, and all of that is permissible within the scope of the will (mashī'ah). This is indicated by His saying: ﴿Our Lord has encompassed all things in knowledge. In Allah we have put our trust. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth﴾, meaning: judge in truth. If it is asked: how did they seek judgment from Allah in truth, when He only judges in truth? It is answered: this is not in the manner of seeking a true judgment; rather it is a description of His judgment as true, for the quality of His judgment is truth. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "My Lord, judge in truth"﴾ in Surat al-Anbiya', ﴿and You are the best of those who decide.﴾

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the eminent ones among his people who disbelieved said, "If you follow Shu'ayb, indeed you would then be losers."﴾ That is, in their religion. ﴿Indeed, you would then be losers.﴾
﴿So the earthquake seized them, and they lay prostrate in their homes.﴾ We have already explained this in the story of Thamud.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 92:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb—it was as if they had never prospered therein.﴾ That is, as if they had never dwelt therein. It is said: "ghanina bi-mawdi' kadhā" (ghanitu bi-mawdi' kadhā), meaning I stayed/resided at such-and-such a place, and al-maghani are the dwelling-places. This is what Tha'lab said. And the poet, who is Hatim al-Ta'i, said:

("We lived for a time in poverty and in wealth, and time gave each of us to drink from its two cups.")

("Our wealth did not add to us any pride before a kinsman, nor did poverty diminish our noble lineage.")

And al-Akhfash said: the meaning of His saying ﴿as if they had never prospered therein﴾ is: as if they had never enjoyed comfort therein. ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb—it was they who were the losers.﴾

So he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and given you sincere advice, so how could I grieve (آسى) i.e., be saddened, over a disbelieving people?"

﴿on a disbelieving people﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 94:

Allah's saying, ﴿And We did not send a prophet into any town without seizing its people with adversity (al-ba's') and hardship (al-darra')﴾.

Ibn Mas'ud said: al-ba's' is poverty, and al-darra' is sickness. This is the meaning of those who said: al-ba's' refers to wealth, and al-darra' refers to the self (person). It was also said: al-ba's' is hunger, and al-darra' is poverty. It was also said: "seizing its people with al-ba's'" means: with wars. ﴿So that they might humble themselves (yatadarra'un)﴾, i.e., so that they (yatadarra'una) might humble themselves.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 95:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We changed the bad condition for good﴾. Mujahid said: "The bad (sayyi'ah) is hardship, and the good (hasanah) is plenty." ﴿Until they multiplied﴾, that is, until they increased in number. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Trim the moustaches and let the beards grow (a'fu al-lihan)", that is, let the beards become abundant. It was also said: ﴿until they multiplied﴾ means until they grew fat.

﴿And they said: Indeed, hardship and ease have touched our fathers﴾, that is, this has been the custom of time from of old for us and for our fathers; so they paid no heed to the hardship that had befallen them. ﴿Then We seized them suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly, ﴿while they did not perceive﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of Allah, We would have opened up for them blessings from the heaven and the earth﴾. He means: from the heaven, through rain, and from the earth, through plants. It was also said: the blessings of the heaven are the answering of supplications, and the blessings of the earth are the easing of needs. ﴿But they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn﴾.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping? Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning while they are at play?﴾ Meaning: that Our punishment comes to them by night and by day. ﴿While they are at play﴾: and everyone who occupies himself with that for which he will not be rewarded is a player (la'ib).

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping? Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning while they are at play?﴾ Meaning: that Our punishment comes to them by night and by day. ﴿While they are at play﴾: and everyone who occupies himself with that for which he will not be rewarded is a player (la'ib).

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do they then feel secure from the plan of Allah?﴾ That is, the punishment of Allah. The "plan of Allah" (makr Allah) is His seizing them suddenly. ﴿None feel secure from the plan of Allah except the people who are losers.﴾

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Or has it not become clear to those who inherit the land﴾ meaning: Or has it not become clear to those who inherit the land after the destruction of its former people ﴿that if We willed, We could afflict them﴾ meaning: that if We willed, We would seize them ﴿for their sins﴾, ﴿and seal upon their hearts so they do not hear﴾, meaning: We would set a seal upon their hearts so that they neither understand nor hear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 101:

God the Exalted said: ﴿Those were the cities; We relate to you some of their news. And their messengers certainly came to them with clear proofs, but they were not going to believe in what they had denied before.﴾ This refers to particular people, whom God knew would not believe. ﴿Thus does God seal the hearts of the disbelievers.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 102:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We found most of them not keeping their covenant﴾, meaning: not fulfilling the covenant. Al-Suddi said: It is the covenant of the Day of the Covenant (al-mithaq), which they did not fulfil. ﴿And indeed, We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient﴾, meaning: We did not find most of them except as defiantly disobedient (fasiqin). It was said: By "fisq" (defiant disobedience) here he meant departing from what their religion requires of fulfilling the covenant, and this was from some of them and not others.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 103:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then after them We sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wronged them thereby﴾. We have already explained that injustice (ẓulm) is placing a thing in other than its proper place, and their wronging [of the signs] was placing disbelief in the place of faith. ﴿So see how was the end of the corrupters﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 104–106:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Moses said, "O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, obligated to say nothing about Allah except the truth."﴾ That is, "obligated to say nothing [about Allah] except the truth." Thus Ibn Mas'ud recited it, and its meaning is: "eager that I not say about Allah except the truth." It is also recited as "ḥaqīqun ʿalayya" (حقيق عليّ), meaning: "it is binding upon me that I not say about Allah except the truth."

﴿I have certainly come to you with a clear proof from your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with me.﴾ That is because Moses intended to take them out toward al-Sham. ﴿He said﴾ – meaning Pharaoh – ﴿"If you have come with a sign, then produce it, if you are of the truthful."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 104–106:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Moses said, "O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, obligated to say nothing about Allah except the truth."﴾ That is, "obligated to say nothing [about Allah] except the truth." Thus Ibn Mas'ud recited it, and its meaning is: "eager that I not say about Allah except the truth." It is also recited as "ḥaqīqun ʿalayya" (حقيق عليّ), meaning: "it is binding upon me that I not say about Allah except the truth."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 104–106:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Moses said, "O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds, obligated to say nothing about Allah except the truth."﴾ That is, "obligated to say nothing [about Allah] except the truth." Thus Ibn Mas'ud recited it, and its meaning is: "eager that I not say about Allah except the truth." It is also recited as "ḥaqīqun ʿalayya" (حقيق عليّ), meaning: "it is binding upon me that I not say about Allah except the truth."

﴿I have certainly come to you with a clear proof from your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with me.﴾ That is because Moses intended to take them out toward al-Sham. ﴿He said﴾ – meaning Pharaoh – ﴿"If you have come with a sign, then produce it, if you are of the truthful."﴾

The Exalted said: ﴿So he cast down his staff﴾. It has been said that an angel gave him that staff, and the staff has a story, which will come in the story of Shu'ayb in Surat al-Qasas (the chapter of the Narratives), God willing.

﴿And behold, it was a manifest serpent (thu'ban)﴾. The thu'ban is the male serpent. In al-Qasas it is related that when Musa (peace and blessings of God be upon him) cast down the staff, it became a huge serpent that filled the palace of Fir'awn (Pharaoh). It has also been said that the distance between its jaws was eighty cubits. It has also been said that it seized the palace of Fir'awn between its fangs, so Fir'awn fled from it, and on that day he was seized by a stomach ailment four hundred times.

Almighty God says: ﴿And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to the onlookers.﴾ It is said: he drew it out from his collar (jayb), and it is said: from under his armpit. ﴿Behold, it was white﴾ with a ray of light like the sun, shining brilliantly, and Musa was dark-complexioned (adam al-lawn).
The Exalted's saying: ﴿The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said: "Indeed, this is a knowing sorcerer."﴾ He means: Musa.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 110:

﴿He wants to drive you out of your land, so what do you advise?﴾ That is: "By what do you advise?" Pharaoh said this to his people. It is also said that this is from the words of the chiefs (al-mala'), who said to Pharaoh and his close circle: "What do you command?" It is also said that they said this to Pharaoh alone, but they spoke in the plural form out of exaltation and honour.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 111:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They said: "Delay him and his brother"﴾. That is: postpone him. Al-irja' (postponement) means delay; it is said: "I postponed (arja'tu) the matter of such-and-such," meaning I delayed it. From this comes the name al-Murji'ah (the Murji'ah, the "Postponers"), who were so named because they postponed action in faith, for they claimed that action is not part of faith.

It is also read as "arjih" without a hamza. It was said that its meaning is likewise delay. Al-Mubarrad said: its meaning is "leave him hoping" (utrukhu yarju). The meaning of all of them is one, for they advised him to postpone his affair and to leave off confronting him. Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that they advised postponing him because there was no illegitimate-born child (walad 'ahir) among them; for had there been an illegitimate-born child among them, they would have advised killing.

﴿And send into the cities gatherers﴾. These are the cities of Upper Egypt (al-Sa'id), and it is above Egypt.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿They will bring you every skilled sorcerer.﴾ And in the narrative: Pharaoh sent the officers of the police (ashab al-shurta) to those cities to gather the sorcerers and bring them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verses 113–114:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the magicians came to Pharaoh﴾. There is an omission in it, meaning: so he sent [for them]; then the magicians came. They differed regarding their number. Ibn 'Abbas said: they were seventy-two men. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: they were twelve thousand. Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said: they were eighty thousand. And the well-known view is that they were seventy thousand.

﴿They said, "Indeed, for us there will surely be a reward if we are the victors." He said, "Yes, and indeed you will be among those brought near."﴾ That is, for you there is the reward; ﴿and indeed you will be among those brought near﴾, meaning: for you there is an elevated status along with the reward.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verses 113–114:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the magicians came to Pharaoh﴾. There is an omission in it, meaning: so he sent [for them]; then the magicians came. They differed regarding their number. Ibn 'Abbas said: they were seventy-two men. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: they were twelve thousand. Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir said: they were eighty thousand. And the well-known view is that they were seventy thousand.

﴿They said, "Indeed, for us there will surely be a reward if we are the victors." He said, "Yes, and indeed you will be among those brought near."﴾ That is, for you there is the reward; ﴿and indeed you will be among those brought near﴾, meaning: for you there is an elevated status along with the reward.
**Allah the Exalted said:** ﴿They said, "O Moses, either you throw, or we will be the ones who throw."﴾ **i.e., the staff.** ﴿Or we will be the ones who throw.﴾ **i.e., ʿaṣīnā.**

﴿He said, "Throw."﴾ Then, when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people. That is, they diverted people's eyes from perceiving the reality of the matter. They did this through *tamwih* (deception by camouflage) and *takhyil* (creating illusion), and this is *sihr* (sorcery).

﴿And they terrified them.﴾ That is, the sorcerers sought to instill awe in the people, so they frightened them. Al-Mubarrad said: the *sin* in *istarhabuhum* is extra, and its meaning is "they frightened them" (*arhabuhum*). ﴿And they produced a great magic.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 117:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We revealed to Musa, "Throw your staff," and behold, it swallowed up what they were falsely fabricating.﴾ It is also read, "talqafu ma ya'fikun" (with the verb lightly pronounced, without the doubled letter), and in the irregular (shadhdh) readings it is read "talqimu" (tulaqqimu). Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "talqimu" with a light pronunciation, and the meaning of all of them is one. Al-talaqquf (swallowing up, seizing quickly) means taking hold of something rapidly, and its meaning is: it swallows up what they falsely fabricate, that is, the false illusions (takhayyul) they were lying about. In the narratives (al-qasas) it is related that the magicians were seventy thousand, each one of them with a staff. They threw their staffs, and they began to move like serpents. Then Musa threw his staff, and it became a serpent, and it swallowed up all of that. The people who were present made for it, and the crowding fell upon them, and twenty-five thousand of them perished in the crush. Then Musa took it, and it became a staff as it had been. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿behold, it swallowed up what they were falsely fabricating.﴾ The poet said:

(You are the staff of Musa, which has never ceased to swallow up what the sorcerer fabricates...)

And another said:

(When Musa came and threw the staff, the magic and the magician were brought to nothing...)

ـ Allah's words, the Exalted: ﴿So the truth was established, and what they had been doing was nullified﴾. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: its meaning is: the truth became manifest, namely, Moses' staff became manifest over their staffs. And it was said: its meaning is: the prophethood of Moses became manifest against the claim of Pharaoh to lordship.
﴿So they were overcome there and returned humbled.﴾ Meaning: abased, humiliated.

And the sorcerers were thrown down prostrating (﴿وَأُلْقِي السَّحَرَةُ سَاجِدِينَ﴾). They differed concerning their prostration. Some of them said: God, may He be exalted, inspired them to prostrate, so they prostrated. It was also said: Moses and Aaron prostrated in thanks to God, may He be exalted, and the sorcerers agreed with them.
﴿They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds."﴾ It is said: When Pharaoh heard this from them, he said, "Have you believed in me?" And they said:

Lord of Moses and Aaron." And Pharaoh said: "You believed in Him before I gave you permission. Indeed, this is a scheme you have plotted in the city." Al-Suddi said: Moses had said to the chief of the magicians: "If I defeat you tomorrow, will you believe in me?" He replied: "I will bring you magic with which I will defeat you, and if you defeat me, I will believe in you." So this is the meaning of Pharaoh's words: "Indeed, this is a scheme you have plotted in the city," i.e., a plan you devised in the city. Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 124:

﴿Then I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, then I will crucify you all together.﴾ He threatened them with these punishments, and they were well known.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 125:

﴿They said, "Indeed, we are to our Lord returning."﴾ So they said this as a consolation for their hearts.

﴿And you do not resent us﴾ — that is, you do not dislike us. It was also said that its meaning is: you do not find fault with us.

﴿except that we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us.﴾ "Our Lord, pour out upon us patience" — that is, send down upon us. ﴿And cause us to die as Muslims.﴾

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the chiefs of Pharaoh's people said﴾. They were called al-mala' (the chiefs) for two reasons. The first is that they filled people's hearts with awe. It was also said that they were called this because they were "full" (mali'in) of what had been entrusted to them.

﴿Will you leave Moses and his people to spread corruption in the land?﴾ By this corruption they meant opposing Pharaoh's command. ﴿And leave you and your gods?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas recited "wa-ilahatika" (and your worship), meaning your worship. It was also said that al-ilahah (the goddess) is the sun, and that Pharaoh worshipped the sun. The poet said:

(We returned from al-La'baa in the afternoon, and the sun-goddess hastened us before we could come back.)

That is, the sun hastened us before it could return. The well-known reading is ﴿and your gods﴾.

Sulayman al-Taymi said: Pharaoh worshipped cows. Al-Suddi said: He had taken idols and said to his people, "These are your gods, and I am the god of the gods." Al-Hasan said: He had hung a cross around his neck and worshipped it. For this reason they said, "and leave you and your gods." This was an incitement by them to Pharaoh against Moses.

﴿He said: We will kill their sons and spare their women﴾. He had previously been doing this, then he stopped, then he returned to it a second time, saying: ﴿We will kill their sons and spare their women, and indeed we are dominant over them.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Moses said to his people, "Seek help in Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants. And the final outcome is for the righteous."﴾ In the irregular readings (al-shawadhdh), it is read as "yūrithuhā" (with a different vowelling). ﴿...and the final outcome is for the righteous﴾ means: in victory and triumph.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 129:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said: We were harmed before you came to us and after you came to us.﴾ Concerning this there are several views.

Al-Hasan said: the harm was by the imposition of the jizya (poll tax). Pharaoh used to take the jizya from them both before the coming of Musa and after it. It was also said: it was by the killing of the sons; he used to kill their sons and spare their women before the coming of Musa, and then he returned to it. Juwaybir mentioned in his tafsir that what was meant was that Pharaoh used to put them to forced labour and make them work until midday, and when Musa came, he made them labour the whole day without wages or anything. Al-Kalbi mentioned that they used to make bricks of clay mixed with Pharaoh's straw before the coming of Musa, and when Musa came, he compelled them to make the bricks with straw from their own possession.

﴿He said: It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and then He will see how you act.﴾ The word "ʿasā" (it may be; perhaps) is a word of hope and expectation. It means: so that He may recompense you according to what He sees actually proceeding from you, not according to what He knows of you in the unseen.

The Exalted said: ﴿And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years [of drought]﴾, meaning: with famine and barrenness.

The Arabs say: "A year (sanah) has come upon us," meaning a year of barrenness. So Allah, the Exalted, seized them with years of drought, ﴿and [We] diminished the fruits, that perhaps they would take heed﴾, meaning: that they would be admonished. This is because hardship softens the hearts and makes them inclined toward Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 131:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But when good came to them﴾, meaning fertility, ﴿they said: "This is ours"﴾, meaning: this has always been our due over time. ﴿But when evil afflicted them﴾, meaning drought, ﴿they ascribed their misfortune to Moses and those with him﴾, meaning they said: "This is from the ill omen of Moses and those with him." ﴿Verily, their omen is with Allah﴾, meaning: ill omen, good fortune, goodness and evil are all from Allah, exalted is He. It was also said that its meaning is: the great ill omen is that which is theirs with Allah, exalted is He, in the Hereafter. The Arabs say: "Good fortune (sa'd) has flown to so-and-so," and "ill omen (shu'm) has flown to so-and-so." ﴿But most of them do not know﴾.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And they said, "Whatever (مَهْمَا, mahmā) sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will never believe you."﴾ That is: مَتى مَا (matā mā), meaning "whenever." {Whatever sign you bring us, to bewitch us with it, we will not be believers in you.}

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 133:

﴿So We sent upon them the flood﴾. Ata said: By the flood he meant a devastating death. It was also said: a great torrent. The story goes that they were rained upon from Saturday to Saturday, until the water reached their collarbones, so that when a man wished to sit, he would drown in the water. They cried out to Musa and said: "Call upon God that He may hold it back from us, and we will believe in you." So he called upon God, and He withheld the rain from them. The earth then produced abundant vegetation that year and became fertile. They said: "This was better for us," but they did not believe and they disbelieved in him. So God sent upon them the locusts, which devoured their crops and vegetation, except for a little. They cried out to Musa that he would call upon God, so that He would remove this from them.

It is related in the reports about Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that locusts became scarce in his time for a year. So he sent a rider toward Yemen, a rider toward Syria, and a rider toward Iraq, to seek out locusts. The rider from Yemen came back with a handful of locusts. Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Allahu akbar! Indeed God has a thousand nations: six hundred on land and four hundred at sea, and the first nation to perish will be the locusts, and then the rest of the nations will follow them."

It is also reported that Maryam asked her Lord and said: "O Lord, feed me meat without blood," so He fed her locusts. And a report says: "Written on the breast of every locust is 'The Greatest Army of God.'"

Returning to the story: when the locusts were lifted from them, they still did not believe. So God sent upon them the lice (qaml). Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada said: the lice are the young locusts, which are the dabā that have no wings. And from Ibn Abbas, in another narration, the lice are the weevils of wheat. Abu Ubayda said: it is the large ticks, and the large tick is also called hamnan. It was also said: the lice are the lice themselves, and it was said: it is nosebleeds. They cried out to Musa, so he called upon God and it was lifted from them, but they did not believe. So He sent upon them the frogs.

It is related in the story that Musa came to the shore of the sea, and pointed with his staff toward the nearest and farthest parts of the sea, and the frogs came out until their houses were filled with them, and they were jumping (qawaz). When a man opened his mouth to speak, a frog would leap into his mouth. Whoever among them slept, when he woke he would find on his body frogs the size of a forearm. Whenever a man spoke, one would hop into his mouth. Then it was lifted from them, but they did not believe. So God made the Nile of Egypt turn to blood upon them, and all of this was specifically for the Copts. The Copt would draw blood from the Nile, while the Children of Israel drew water, so that from a single vessel the Copt would drink fresh blood and the Israelite water. That is the meaning of His words: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood, and the locusts, and the lice, and the frogs, and the blood, as distinct signs﴾. Its detail is that each of these punishments lasted a week, and there was a month between each two punishments. ﴿But they were arrogant, and they were a criminal people﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 134:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And when the punishment (al-rijz) befell them﴾. It has been said: He meant by it the punishment mentioned earlier. And it has been said: It is the punishment of the plague (al-ta'un). Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Seventy thousand of them died of the plague in a single day. Al-rijz means al-rijs (filth, abomination): the punishment.

﴿They said: O Musa, call upon your Lord for us by what He has promised you (bima 'ahida 'indak)﴾, meaning: by answering your supplication. ﴿If you remove from us the punishment, we will surely believe in you and send with you the Children of Israel﴾, for he intended to take them out toward al-Sham.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 135:

﴿So when We removed from them the punishment until a term which they were to reach, behold, they broke their word.﴾ That refers to the drowning in the sea (al-yamm). ﴿Behold, they broke their word.﴾ That is, they violated the covenant.

So We took vengeance on them and drowned them in the sea, because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them. ﴿So We took vengeance on them and drowned them in the sea, because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.﴾ And the story of the drowning will come in its proper place, God willing, Exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 137:

﴿And We made the people who had been oppressed inherit the eastern and western parts of the earth, which We had blessed.﴾ It is said that by this He meant the land of Egypt and Syria. It is also said that He meant Syria alone, and it is said that He meant Jordan and Palestine. His words ﴿which We had blessed﴾ mean: with fertility and abundance.

﴿And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience.﴾ That "good word" is His promise which He made to them, found in His words: ﴿And We wished to show favour to those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and make them the inheritors﴾. So when He made them inherit those lands and fulfilled that promise to them, He said: ﴿the good word of your Lord was fulfilled﴾, meaning His promise to them was carried out. He called it "good" (ḥusnā) because it was in accordance with what they loved. ﴿And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been making and building﴾, meaning: We brought that destruction upon them. ﴿And what they had been erecting﴾ (i.e., what they were building and roofing, out of arrogance and haughtiness).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 138:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people devoted to idols of theirs.﴾ That is, they were constantly devoted to the worship of those idols. They were a people from the Amalekites, whom the Children of Israel saw devoted to their idols. ﴿They said, "O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods."﴾ This was not, on the part of the Children of Israel, a doubt about the oneness (wahdaniyyah) of God, may He be exalted. Rather, its meaning was: "Make for us something that we may venerate, and through venerating it draw near to God, may He be exalted." They thought that this would not harm their religion, and this was from the extent of their ignorance.

{﴿He said, "Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 139:

Indeed, these people, what they are in is (i.e., destroyed, ruined) ( ﴿and what they used to do is void﴾

(He said), meaning Musa: ﴿Should I seek for you a god other than Allah?﴾ That is: should I seek for you a god that you would exalt, other than Allah? ﴿And He has favoured you over the worlds.﴾

And in the well-known report: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned from Hunayn, he passed by a tree called Dhat Anwat, around which some of the Bedouins were devoted and venerating it, and they had hung their weapons upon it. His companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, make for us a Dhat Anwat just as they have a Dhat Anwat." He (ﷺ) said: "Allahu Akbar! This is just like what the people of Musa said to Musa: ﴿Make for us a god just as they have gods.﴾"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 141:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [recall] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment﴾. That is, they made you taste the worst of torment. We have already mentioned the meaning of this in surah al-Baqarah.

﴿They slaughtered your sons﴾, meaning: your young sons, ﴿and spared your women. And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾. It was said that its meaning is: in their torturing you there was a great trial from your Lord. And it was said: in Our delivering you there was ﴿a great trial from your Lord﴾, that is, a blessing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 142:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten﴾. The exegetes said: They are the days of Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten of Dhu al-Hijjah. ﴿So the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights﴾. If it is said: Mentioning the thirty and the ten makes mentioning the forty unnecessary, so what is the meaning of this repetition? It is said: He repeated it for emphasis. It is also said: The benefit of His saying ﴿So the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights﴾ is to cut off the thoughts from an addition. For when He first fixed thirty, then added ten to it, perhaps another addition would occur to the thoughts, so He mentioned it to cut off thoughts from an addition. And He mentioned the thirty at the beginning and the ten in detail, so that it would be known that the appointed time was thus in detail: thirty of Dhu al-Qa'dah and ten of Dhu al-Hijjah.

And in the narrative: God, exalted is He, commanded Moses to fast thirty days, then come to the Mount (al-Tur) to speak with him; so he fasted thirty days, night and day.

And in some exegeses: He fasted thirty days, and the smell of his mouth changed, so he took the leaves of the carob tree and chewed them, so that the smell of his mouth would go away. So God, exalted is He, commanded him to fast ten more days, so that the smell would return. The completion of the story is in the second verse.

﴿And Moses said to his brother Aaron: Take my place among my people﴾: He appointed him as his successor over his people. ﴿And act rightly﴾: i.e., be gentle. ﴿And do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾: i.e., do not follow their opinions and desires.

(﴿142﴾) ﴿And when Moses came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said: My Lord, show me that I may look at You. He said: You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me. So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain, He made it crumble, and Moses fell down unconscious﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 143:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Musa came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him﴾, meaning: at the time that was set for him, as we have explained. ﴿His Lord spoke to him.﴾ In the narrative: when Allah, exalted is He, summoned him to the side of the Mount (al-Tur), sent down a darkness extending over seven farsakh, drove away Satan from him, removed the two angels from him, and spoke to him until He made him hear and understand. In the narrative: Jibril was with him, but he did not hear what his Lord said.

﴿He said: My Lord, show me Yourself that I may look upon You.﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: there is an omission in it, and its meaning is: show me Yourself, that I may look upon You. If someone says: how did he ask for the vision when he knew that Allah, mighty and majestic, cannot be seen in this world? Al-Hasan said: longing overwhelmed him, so he asked for the vision. It was also said: he asked for the vision, supposing that it was permissible to see Him in this world.

﴿He said: You will not see Me.﴾ Those who deny the vision (of Allah) cite this statement as evidence, but there is no proof for them in it. This is because He did not say, "I am not seen," which would have been an argument for them; and because He did not attribute to him ignorance in asking for the vision, as his people were attributed to him when they said, "Make for us a god just as they have gods," which was not permissible. As for the meaning of His saying ﴿You will not see Me﴾, it means: at present, or in this world.

﴿But look at the mountain; if it remains firmly in its place, then you will see Me.﴾ Its meaning: make the mountain between you and Me, for it is stronger than you; if it remains firmly in its place, then you will see Me. In this there is evidence that it is possible to be seen, because He did not make the vision conditional upon something impossible to exist; for the mountain's remaining firm while He manifests Himself to it is not impossible, by His giving it the power to remain firm while manifesting.

﴿So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain﴾, that is, appeared to the mountain. It was said: He made for the mountain sight and created in it life; then He manifested Himself to it, and it became mindful of Him. Hammad ibn Salamah narrated from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah, exalted is He, manifested Himself to the mountain to the extent of the joint of the little finger." Then Thabit placed his thumb on the joint of his little finger. It was said to him: "Do you say this?" He said: "Anas says it and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said it, and I do not say it myself!" And he struck the chest of the questioner. In some narrations: "He manifested Himself to the mountain to the extent of the wing of a mosquito or less."

﴿He made it crumble to dust.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: it became dust. Al-Hasan and Sufyan said: it sank into the earth. In some tafsir works: it became six mountains: three in Makkah, namely Thawr, Thabir and Hira, and three in Madinah: Radwa, Uhud and Warqan. It was also said: the mountain was uprooted from its base and fell into the sea, and it continues to move in it until the Day of Resurrection.

As for the linguistic aspect: al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of His saying ﴿made it crumble to dust﴾ is that it was made crushed and pulverized. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "ja'alahu dakkaa'" with a long vowel, from the saying "ard dakkaa'" when there are protrusions and elevated places in it like hilltops; and al-dakkawat are the hills of the earth. Its meaning: He made it like elevated land, and it went out of being a mountain.

His saying: ﴿And Musa fell down unconscious (sa'qan)﴾. Qatadah said: sa'qan means dead, for he had died at that very hour. Al-Hasan and Ibn Abbas said: he fell down in a swoon. This is more fitting to the context, because He said ﴿So when he regained consciousness, he said: Glory be to You﴾, and this is glorification. ﴿I have repented to You﴾, that is, from asking for the vision before permission was given. ﴿And I am the first of the believers﴾, that is, I am the first of the believers that one who sees You manifest in this world does not remain in his place. It was also said its meaning is: I am the first of the believers that You will not be seen in this world.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 144:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Musa, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech﴾. If someone says: He has given others messages too, so what is the meaning of His saying: ﴿I have chosen you above the people by My messages﴾? It is said: Since the giving of messages was not general with respect to people, His saying ﴿I have chosen you above the people by My messages﴾ is correct, even though others share it with him. This is like a man saying: "I have singled you out for my counsel," even though he consults others as well; but since consultation is not general, the statement stands. ﴿So take what I have given you and be among the grateful﴾ for what I have bestowed upon you of giving you the message and the speech. This verse is a consolation to Musa, peace be upon him, when he asked to see (God) and was not granted it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 145:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets﴾, by which He meant the Torah. In a report: "Indeed Allah, may He be exalted, created Adam with His own hand, wrote the Torah with His own hand, and planted the tree of Tuba with His own hand."

The scholars differed concerning those tablets. Al-Hasan said: the tablets were of wood. Mujahid said: they were of green chrysolite (zabarjad akhdar). Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they were of a red ruby (yaqut hamra'). Abu al-'Aliyah said: they were of beryl (bard). It has also been said: the tablets and the Torah were sent down with writing on them like the engraving of a seal.

﴿of every thing an admonition﴾, that is: a reminder. The real meaning of admonition (mau'izah) is reminding and warning against what its consequence is feared. ﴿and a detailed explanation of every thing﴾, that is: a clarification of what is lawful and unlawful, and what they were commanded and what they were forbidden. ﴿So take it with strength﴾, that is: with earnestness and diligence. It has also been said its meaning is: with the strength of the heart.

﴿And enjoin your people to take the best of it﴾. Qatrab said: that is, "by its goodness" (bi-husnaha). Know that the best (al-ahsan) is what contains the obligatory duties (al-fara'id al-maktubah) and the recommended supererogatory acts (al-nawafil al-mandub ilayha), for these are the best; as for the good (al-hasan), it is what is permissible (mubah). It has also been said that the meaning of His saying ﴿they take the best of it﴾ is: the better of the two matters in every thing, such as pardon being better than retaliation, and patience being better than avenging oneself. ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾. Qasama ibn Zuhayr read "sa-uwrithukum" (I will make you inherit), from inheritance (al-tawrith). According to this reading its meaning is: I will make you inherit the land of Egypt. As for the well-known reading "sa-urikum" (I will show you), Mujahid and a group said: I will show you Hell. It has also been said that it means the places where the disbelievers fell. Qatadah said: by "the abode of the defiantly disobedient" is meant al-Sham (Syria), in the sense: I will show you therein what I destroyed of the towns of the disbelievers before you, because Musa set out with them toward al-Sham.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 146:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right﴾. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna said: its meaning is, "I will prevent them from understanding the Qur'an." Al-Zajjaj said: its estimated sense is, "I will turn them away from accepting My signs." As for arrogance (takabbur), it is seeking superiority without entitlement.

﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it; and if they see the way of guidance, they will not take it as a way.﴾ Abu 'Abd al-Rahman 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' recited: "sabil al-rashad" (with the alif), and the variant "sabil al-rushd" (with a dammah on the shin, as in "al-rushd"), and he also recited "sabil al-rushd" with the shin pronounced as it is in the standard reading. Al-rushd and al-rashad are one and the same, and it means righteousness (al-salah).

﴿And if they see the way of error, they will take it as a way⁠—﴾ meaning the way of misguidance ﴿that is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them⁠﴾, because when they did not reflect upon the Qur'an, it was as if they were heedless of it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 147:

﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, their deeds have become worthless.﴾ That is: their deeds became null and void. ﴿Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 148:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the people of Musa took, after him, from their ornaments﴾, and it is read "min huliyyihim" (from their ornaments), ﴿a calf, a body having a lowing sound﴾. That is: a body that has a lowing sound. It is also read in the irregular readings (shadh) "lahuju'ar" (it has a bellowing), which has the same meaning as "khuwar" (lowing).

Regarding the narrative: when Musa, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, prepared to go out to the Tur (Mount Sinai), he said to his people: "I will return to you after thirty days." When he did not return to them after the thirty, they assumed that he had died. As-Samiri (al-Samiri) was obeyed among the Children of Israel, and he was a goldsmith. He said to them: "Gather for me what you took of the ornaments of the people of Pharaoh, and I will make something for you." They handed over to him what they had taken of the ornaments, and he fashioned the calf from it. Al-Hasan said: As-Samiri had seen Jibril (Gabriel) on the day Pharaoh drowned, mounted on a horse, so he took a handful of dust from the print of the horse's hoof.

Ikrimah said: It was cast into his heart that whatever he threw that handful of dust upon, that thing would come to life by it. This was because he saw the places where the horse's hoof had touched immediately become alive and sprout. So when he had shaped the calf, it was cast into his heart that he should put that handful into its mouth, and he did so; it came to life, becoming flesh and blood of gold, and it had a lowing sound, for it lowed. Then as-Samiri said: ﴿This is your god and the god of Musa, but he has forgotten﴾, as will come in its narrative in Surat Ta-Ha. It was also said that it lowed only once, and it was said that it lowed frequently, as a cow lows, and whenever it lowed they prostrated to it, and whenever it fell silent they raised their heads.

Some of the exegetes said: no life was ever put into it at all, and it had no real lowing; rather, what they heard of the lowing was by trickery. The first view, however, is the correct one. Then they differed concerning the number of those who worshipped the calf. Al-Hasan said: all of them worshipped it except Harun alone. It was also said, and this is the more correct view: all of them worshipped it except Harun and twelve thousand men among them.

﴿Did they not see that it does not speak to them, nor guide them to a way?﴾ This is evidence that Allah is the Speaker, who has always been and always will be, because He argued from the calf's lack of speech to the negation of its divinity.

﴿Nor guide them to a way﴾: that is, a path. ﴿They took it, and they were wrongdoers﴾, by placing divinity in other than its proper place.

"The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when they regretted and saw that they had gone astray﴾. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say, "So-and-so fell into regret (suqita fi yadihi)" when he remains remorseful and bewildered over what has escaped him, as if the regret had landed in his hand. ﴿They said: If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.﴾"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 150:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved﴾. Abu al-Darda' said: "al-asaf" is intense anger. It was also said: "al-asaf" is intense sorrow. It seems that Musa returned remorseful and sorrowful, saying: "Would that I had been among them, so that what befell them would not have befallen them."

﴿He said: Evil is what you did in my absence after me﴾, meaning: (evil is what you did in my absence). ﴿Did you rush ahead of your Lord's command?﴾ Its meaning: did you precede your Lord's command, that is, by your act which you committed without your Lord's command. It was also said its meaning is: you hastened your Lord's promise.

﴿And he threw down the tablets﴾. He had been carrying them, and he threw them on the ground out of intense anger. In the exegesis it is related that when he threw them, some of them went back up to heaven and two tablets remained. What had been in them of news of the unseen returned, and what remained was the admonition and the rulings concerning the lawful and the unlawful. It was also said: when he threw down the tablets, some of them broke, so Musa bound them with gold. ﴿And he seized his brother by the head﴾, meaning Harun. There is an omission in it, and its implied sense is: he seized his brother by the hair of his head ﴿dragging him towards himself. He said: Son of my mother﴾, meaning Harun said to Musa: "Son of my mother." It is read with a kasra and with a fatha on the mim. As for with a kasra on the mim, its meaning is: O son of my mother. The poet said: (O son of my mother, and O brother of my soul, you have left me to a grave matter.)

As for with a fatha on the mim, the reasoning for the fatha is that his saying "ibn umm" is two words, but they are like one word, like their saying "Hadramawt" and "Ba'labakk": one of the two names was compounded with the other, so it remained in the accusative as a particle of specification.

﴿Indeed the people deemed me weak and nearly killed me﴾. In the story: when the appointed time of thirty nights had passed, Harun would stand among them as a preacher, preaching every day and weeping, and saying: "I implore you by God, do not worship the calf, for Musa will return tomorrow, God willing." He continued doing this for three days. When he did not return after the three days, they said: "He has died," so they left him and turned to worshipping the calf. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Indeed the people deemed me weak and nearly killed me, so do not let the enemies gloat over me﴾. Gloating is doing what pleases the enemy. ﴿And do not place me with the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: do not place me with the disbelievers and among them.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my brother﴾. This means: for what I did to my brother, seizing his hair and dragging him, though he was innocent. His words ﴿and my brother﴾ mean: for whatever shortcoming befell him, if he did fall short. ﴿And admit us into Your mercy, for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 7, verse 152:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who took the calf﴾ contains an ellipsis (ḥadhf), and its full sense is: "took the calf as a god." ﴿Wrath from their Lord and humiliation will reach them in the life of this world.﴾ It was said: by "humiliation" he meant the jizya (poll-tax). And it was said: he meant that some of them would say to one another, while knowing that they had gone astray. ﴿Thus do We recompense the fabricators.﴾ That is, every one who fabricates against Allah. Among the well-known sayings concerning this verse is that of Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, who said: "This applies to every innovator (mubtadi') until the Day of Resurrection."
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And those who committed evil deeds and then repented after them and believed - indeed, your Lord, after them, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is: after repentance (tawbah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 154:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And when the anger subsided from Musa﴾. Mu'awiya ibn Qurra recited: "And when the anger quieted (wa lamma sakan) from Musa", and in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b it reads: "And when the anger was lifted (wa lamma sayyara) from Musa", and in the codex of Hafsa it reads: "Verily the anger was stilled (wa innama uskita) from Musa". The meaning of all of them is one, namely: the anger subsided (sakana) from Musa. Al-sukut (silence) and al-iskat (stilling) are well known, and it is said: a man is "sukayt" (very silent) if he is much given to silence.

﴿He took up the tablets﴾, and that is because he had thrown them down and then took them up. ﴿And in their inscription﴾: the scholars differed concerning this. Some of them said: it means the tablets themselves, for they have an original from which they were copied (nusikhat), namely the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). It was also said: when Musa threw down the tablets, they broke, so he copied another inscription from them, and this is what is meant by His words: ﴿And in their inscription is guidance and mercy﴾, that is, guidance from misguidance and mercy from punishment, ﴿for those who fear their Lord﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 155:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Musa chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment﴾. There is an ellipsis in it; that is, "from among his people." In this there is evidence that not all of them worshipped the calf, and this is the more sound view. They differed as to why he chose them. Some said: he chose them so that they could make excuse before God for the worship of those who worshipped the calf. It was also said: he chose them so that they might hear the speech of God, for they asked Musa for that. ﴿Then, when the quake seized them﴾. Mujahid said: the earth shook beneath them, so they died. It was also said: a trembling and convulsion occurred in their limbs, to the point that some of them nearly separated from others. It was also said: He destroyed them only as a punishment for their request to see God openly.

(He said: "My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me as well.") This is because Musa thought that God, exalted is He, had destroyed them only because of the worship of the calf by those people, and he feared that the Children of Israel would accuse him, saying: "Musa killed them." So he said: ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before﴾, meaning: at the worship of the calf, before I brought them. ﴿And me as well﴾, for the killing of the Copt whom Musa had killed. It was also said: he meant by this the eternal will, as though he entrusted their destruction to His will, that is: "If You had willed from eternity to destroy them and me, and whoever is in the world, then no one has any objection against You."

﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish ones among us did?﴾ They differed about how he could say, "Will You destroy us for what the foolish ones among us did?", while he knew that God, exalted is He, does not destroy anyone for the sin of another. Some said: this is an interrogative in the sense of denial, and this is the view of Ibn al-Anbari, that is: "Do not destroy us for the deed of the foolish ones." This is like a man saying to his companion: "Do you act ignorantly toward me while I am forbearing?" meaning: "I am not forbearing." And it is said in the proverb: "A swelling like the swelling of a camel? And death in the house of the Salulite woman?" meaning: this will never happen. And the poet said:

(Do you forget, when she polishes her cheeks with a twig of bisham, watered with bisham?)

meaning: you do not forget. It was also said: it is an interrogative in the sense of affirmation, and what is intended by it is a request, as though he were asking: "Will You destroy us for what the foolish ones among us did?"

﴿It is but Your trial﴾, that is, Your test, ﴿by which You lead astray whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of those who forgive﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 156:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And ordain for us﴾, i.e., decree for us ﴿in this world a good [portion]﴾, which is blessing and well-being, ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾, i.e., and in the Hereafter a good [portion], so it is omitted.

﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾, i.e., we have repented to You. Abu Wajza al-Sa'di read "hudna ilayk" with a kasra on the ha', meaning: we have inclined to You. ﴿He said, "My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will"﴾. This is in accordance with the view of the People of the Sunnah, for God, may He be exalted, has the right to afflict with His punishment whomever He wills of His servants, whether they have sinned or not. Some of the Qadariyya distorted the text and read "my punishment - I afflict with it whom I will" as "whom has done evil" (asa'a, from the verb of evil-doing), but this is nothing.

﴿And My mercy encompasses all things﴾. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: His mercy encompassed the righteous and the wicked in this world, while it is for the God-fearing on the Day of Resurrection. And in the reports: "Mercy is recorded for the righteous and the wicked in this world."

{So I will write it for those who fear God, and give zakat, and those who believe in Our signs.}

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 7, verse 157:

Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet (ﷺ), the unlettered one (al-ummi). This is a great virtue for this Ummah. Musa (peace be upon him) asked that mercy be prescribed for him and his people, and He prescribed it for the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

It is related in the reports that Musa (peace be upon him) said: "O Lord, I find in the Torah a nation who enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in Allah. Make them of my Ummah." Allah, the Exalted, said: "That is the Ummah of Ahmad." He said: "O Lord, I find in the Torah a nation whose charities are in their bellies, meaning their poor eat them, whereas the charities of his people and those before them were consumed by fire. Make them of my Ummah." He, the Exalted, said: "That is the Ummah of Ahmad." He said: "O Lord, I find in the Torah a nation who are the last of people to emerge and the first of people to enter Paradise. Make them of my Ummah." He said: "That is the Ummah of Ahmad." He said: "O Lord, I find in the Torah a nation whose Gospels are in their chests, who observe the sun and the times for Your remembrance. Make them of my Ummah." He said: "That is the Ummah of Ahmad." He said: "O Lord, I find in the Torah a nation that when one of them intends a good deed, it is recorded for him as a good deed, and if he does it, it is recorded for him as ten up to seven hundred times; and when he intends an evil deed, it is not recorded against him, and if he does it, it is recorded against him as one. Make them of my Ummah." He said: "That is the Ummah of Ahmad." Then he threw down the Tablets and said: "O Allah, make me of the Ummah of Muhammad."

This is another account, mentioned as the reason for his throwing down the Tablets, but the first is more evident.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet, the unlettered one﴾ refers to Muhammad (ﷺ), and we have already explained the meaning of "unlettered" (al-ummi) earlier.

﴿Whom they find written﴾ i.e., described ﴿with them in the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins on them what is right, forbids them what is wrong, makes lawful for them the good things﴾, meaning what the disbelievers had made unlawful, such as the sawa'ib, the wasa'il, the bahair and the hawami, and the like, ﴿and makes unlawful for them the evil things﴾, such as carrion, blood, the flesh of swine and the like, ﴿and relieves them of their burden﴾. The burden (al-isr) is everything that weighs heavily on a person, whether a saying or an action; and al-isr is a heavy covenant. Their burden was that Allah, the Exalted, made their repentance dependent on killing themselves. ﴿And the shackles that were upon them﴾: this includes what was upon them of cutting off the place of impurity from a garment with scissors, and that washing it did not suffice for them; that their prayers were valid only in churches; that it was not permitted for them to accept blood-money for a slain person, but retaliation (qisas) was required; and that they were obliged to cut off the offending limbs, and had no alternative. He called them shackles because they were like a collar around their necks.

﴿So those who believe in him﴾, i.e., in Muhammad, ﴿and honour him﴾, i.e., magnify him, ﴿and help him, and follow the light that was sent down with him﴾, which is the Qur'an, ﴿those are the successful.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 158:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, the One to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death. So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him that you may be guided.﴾

Meaning: Muhammad believes in Allah and in the Qur'an. And it is read "wa-kalimatihi" (and His word, singular). It was said: it is also the Qur'an. And some of them said: by the "word" he meant 'Isa (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 159:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and by it act justly.﴾ Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: "These are a people at the farthest east, beyond China, at the rising place of the sun. They were upon the law of Musa, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, until Muhammad was sent. When Muhammad was sent, they believed in him, and they were upon the truth from the time of Musa until the time of Muhammad, peace be upon them both." It was also said: they are those among the Jews who embraced Islam in the time of the Prophet, such as Ibn Suriya (Ibn Suriya) and Ibn Salam, and others like them. The first view is more apparent.

As for His saying: ﴿and by it act justly﴾, meaning: they stand firm upon the truth and justice.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 160:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We divided them into twelve tribes, as nations﴾. That is: We separated them into divisions. And His saying: ﴿twelve﴾ is said in the language as "ithnatay ʿashrata" with the shin vowelled with a kasra and with the shin pronounced with a jazm (sukun). What is permissible in the Qur'an is the jazm on the shin. If it is asked: why did He not say "ithnay ʿashara asbatan" in the masculine? It is said: He mentioned it in the feminine because it refers back to "umam" (nations).

They said: In the verse there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) and its sense is: "And We divided them into tribes (asbatan), nations (umaman), twelve." It has also been said that there is an ellipsis (hadhf), and its sense is: "And We divided them into twelve groups (firqah), tribes, nations," so that "asbatan" is a substitute (badal) for "firqah." We have already explained that the asbat among the sons of Isaac are like the qabail (tribes) among the sons of Ishmael. And they recited, concerning the sibt (tribe):

("ʿAlī and the three of his sons... they are the asbat, there is no concealment regarding them")

("So a sibt of Iman and Birr, and a sibt whose absence is Karbala'")

That is: karb (grief) and bala' (affliction).

﴿And We revealed to Musa, when his people asked him for water: Strike the rock with your staff﴾. We have already explained this in Surat al-Baqarah.

﴿So there gushed forth from it twelve springs﴾. That is: they burst forth. ﴿Every people knew their drinking place. And We shaded them with the clouds, and sent down upon them the manna and the quails: "Eat of the good things with which We have provided you." And they did not wrong Us, but they wronged themselves﴾. Its interpretation has already passed in Surat al-Baqarah.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when it was said to them, "Dwell in this town and eat from it wherever you wish, and say, 'Relief [hittah],' and enter the gate prostrating; We will forgive you your sins. We will increase [the reward of] the doers of good."﴾ It is also read as "khaṭī'atikum" (your errors), and both are one and the same. We have explained this also in Surat al-Baqarah.

﴿So those who did wrong among them changed the saying into another word than that which had been said to them, so We sent upon them a plague from the sky, because they had been doing wrong﴾. Al-Sam'ani: "We have already explained the meaning of this substitution," ﴿so those who did wrong among them changed the saying into another word than that which had been said to them, so We sent upon them a plague from the sky﴾ (that is, a punishment from the sky) ﴿because they had been doing wrong﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 163:

God's words, ﴿And ask them about the town﴾, are a question of reproach and rebuke, not a question seeking information. Scholars differed about which town this was. Ibn 'Abbas said it was Aylah (al-Ayla). al-Zuhri said it was Tiberias of Syria (Tabariyyat al-Sham). It was also said that it was Madyan, ﴿which was by the sea﴾, meaning adjacent to the sea, ﴿when they transgressed on the Sabbath﴾, meaning they exceeded God's command concerning the Sabbath. God, may He be exalted, had forbidden them to do any work on the Sabbath other than worship.

﴿When their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day﴾, meaning visibly. This is what Ibn 'Abbas said, and from it comes the word "shawari' (streets)," because of their visibility. It was also said that it derives from "shuru'" (entering), meaning entry, so the sense is that this town had a gulf of the sea beside it, and the fish would enter it on the Sabbath day but would not enter it on the other days. In the narration: they would come to them like white fat rams on the Sabbath day, approaching their doors, and then none of them would be seen on any day other than the Sabbath. This is God's words: ﴿and on the day they do not keep the Sabbath, they do not come to them﴾. al-Hasan recited "la yasbituna" with a dammah on the yaa', meaning they do not enter upon the Sabbath, whereas the well-known reading is "la yasbituna," meaning they do not hold the Sabbath in honor. It is said: "asbata" when one enters the Sabbath, and "sabata" when one honors the Sabbath. That is, "and on a day they do not honor the Sabbath, they do not come to them." According to al-Hasan's reading: "and on a day they do not enter the Sabbath, they do not come to them." This was a trial from God, may He be exalted, for them, as He said: ﴿Thus did We test them﴾, meaning We examine them, ﴿because they used to defy (God's command)﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 7, verse 164:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And when a community among them said, "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?"﴾ In the narrative: they resorted to a trick for fishing. They would set out the nets on Friday so that the fish would be caught in them on Saturday, and then they would take them on Sunday. It is also said that Satan whispered to them that Allah, Exalted is He, had not forbidden them from fishing on this day, but had only forbidden them from eating [the fish]; so they fished on Saturday. Then they split into three groups: a group that fished, a group that forbade and enjoined what is right, and a group that remained silent. The two groups said to the disobedient group: "We will not live with you in a town where you have disobeyed Allah." So we separated from the town and went out. When they woke in the morning, they came to the gate of the town, but they did not open the gate for them. So they brought a ladder; when they climbed up by the ladder, they saw that they had been transformed into apes. Qatadah said: "They had tails, and they ran about."

As for His words: ﴿And when a community among them said﴾ — this is the silent group, who said to the group that forbade: ﴿Why do you admonish a people﴾, meaning the disobedient group, ﴿whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ They replied: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord﴾, meaning: our admonition is an excuse. That is because we have been commanded to enjoin what is right, so we presented this command to them, even if they did not accept it, so that it would be an excuse for us before Allah, Exalted is He. It is also read "maʿdhiratan" (معذرة) in the accusative, meaning: we offer an excuse (naʿtadhir maʿdhiratan) to your Lord. ﴿And perhaps they will fear Allah.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 165:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, meaning: they abandoned what they had been reminded of. It was said: they used to hunt for seven days, and it was said: they had hunted only on one day.

﴿We rescued those who forbade evil﴾, meaning: the group that forbade (the sin). ﴿And We seized those who did wrong with a dreadful punishment﴾, meaning: the disobedient group. So We seized them with a dreadful punishment, on the pattern of fa'il (ba'is). Ba'is is on the pattern of fa'il, ba'is is on the pattern of fa'l, and ba'is is on the pattern of fa'lal; all are one, and its meaning is: a severe punishment. Ibn 'Abbas said: a punishment with no mercy in it.

﴿Because they were defiantly disobedient (yafsuqun)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: I do not know whether the disobedient group has perished, and the group that forbade has been saved, and I do not know the state of the silent group.

'Ikrimah said: I kept reciting it to him, meaning from the verses, degree by degree, and he (meaning Ibn 'Abbas) was watching me, until he said: the silent group was saved, and he clothed me with a garment for that. For 'Ikrimah would speak with him about the verse and derive evidence from its outward meaning, until the proof became clear to Ibn 'Abbas of the salvation of the silent group. Among the evidence in the outward meaning of the verse is that He said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, and that group did not forget that. The second is that He said: ﴿We rescued those who forbade evil﴾, while the silent group had forbidden by way of warning, by their saying: "Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy?"

The third is that He said: ﴿And We seized those who did wrong﴾, meaning by hunting on the Sabbath; and that group did not do wrong by hunting. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: two groups were saved, and one group perished.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when they persisted in defiance of what they had been forbidden, We said to them, "Be apes, despised and driven away."﴾ This is a command of creation (amr takwin), and His saying ﴿khasi'in﴾ means: removed far away (mub'adin).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 167:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when your Lord declared﴾, meaning: "your Lord made it known (a'lama)." The poet said:

(Ta'adhdhana in sharr al-nas hayy... yunadi min sha'arihim Yasar)

Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: "your Lord swore an oath (ta'alla) and took an oath (halafa), ﴿that He would surely send against them, until the Day of Resurrection, those who would afflict them with an evil punishment﴾, meaning: He would make them taste an evil punishment, which is the jizya (poll tax). It was also said: it is the killing by Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) of them. If someone says: how can a punishment be sent against them when he has destroyed them? It was also said: He meant by it upon their sons and those who come after them. ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾.

"Their dispersal throughout the land into communities": ﴿And We divided them in the earth into nations﴾ — meaning: We split them into factions, and the sense is that We scattered the affair of the Jews so that they do not unite upon one word. ﴿Among them are the righteous﴾ — meaning those among them who embraced Islam. ﴿And among them are others than that﴾ — meaning those who remained upon disbelief.

﴿And We tested them﴾ — meaning We examined them ﴿with good things and bad things﴾ — meaning with abundance and scarcity, and with good and evil, ﴿that they might return﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 169:

The words of His, the Exalted: ﴿Then there succeeded them a succession﴾. Know that al-khalf (succession, later generation) is used both in dispraise and in praise, but when used without qualification, al-khalf (with a sukun on the lam) is for praise, and al-khalaf (with a fatha on the lam) is for blame. The poet said:

(For us, the former of them toward You, and for us the latter, following them in obedience to God.)

Here it is used in dispraise, and by it he means the descendants of those people already mentioned, the people of the Sabbath. ﴿They inherited the Book﴾, meaning the Book passed down to them. ﴿They take the goods of this lower life﴾, meaning the fleeting trappings of the world. The world was only called "dunya" (the lower, nearer one) because it is nearer to creatures than the Hereafter; for this reason He said: ﴿the goods of this lower life﴾, and they say, "It will be forgiven us." This is their deception concerning God, the Exalted. In a hadith: "The shrewd person is one who holds himself to account and works for what comes after death, and the foolish person is one who follows his desires and wishes for forgiveness from God." ﴿And if a similar good should come to them, they would take it.﴾ Mujahid said: He describes them as persisting in sin.
