It was also said that its meaning is: they take, taking after taking, not caring whether it is lawful or unlawful, but taking without inquiry.

﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they would not say about God except the truth?﴾ That is: a covenant was taken from them that they would not say about God other than the truth, in the Torah. ﴿And they studied what is in it﴾, that is, they knew it by study, as said by al-Dahhak. Darasa al-kitab (to study the Book) means reading it again and again. ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear God. Will you not reason?﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer﴾. It is said: this refers to the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). And it is said: it refers to those among the Jews who embraced Islam, who hold fast to the Qur'an and establish prayer. ﴿Indeed, We do not allow the reward of the reformers to be lost.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 171:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [recall] when We raised the mountain above them as if it were a canopy﴾. "Nataqna" means: We raised the mountain above them. This has been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah. ﴿And they thought that it was going to fall upon them﴾: meaning, they became certain. "Al-zann" (assumption) here means "al-yaqin" (certainty). It was also said: what overcame their assumption was that it would fall upon them. ﴿Take what We have given you with determination, and remember what is in it, that you may become righteous﴾. We have already mentioned the story in Surat al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 172:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾. There is a certain difficulty in this verse, and its explanation and interpretation are found in the reports (al-akhbar). Malik related in the Muwatta', with its chain of transmission, from Muslim ibn Yasar al-Juhani, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was asked about this verse, and he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed Allah, may He be exalted, wiped the back of Adam and brought forth from it his descendants, and said: These are for Paradise, and they will act with the deeds of the people of Paradise. Then He wiped the back of Adam and brought forth descendants, and said: These are the people of the Fire, and they will act with the deeds of the people of the Fire.' It was said: 'O Messenger of Allah, then what is the point of deeds?' He said: 'Indeed Allah, may He be exalted, when He creates a people for Paradise, employs them in the deeds of the people of Paradise until He admits them to Paradise, and when He creates a people for the Fire, employs them in the deeds of the people of the Fire until He admits them to the Fire.'"

The well-known view, which the majority of the exegetes hold concerning the meaning of the verse, is that Allah, may He be exalted, wiped the right side of the back of Adam and brought forth from it descendants white like specks (dharr), moving about. Then He wiped the left side of the back of Adam and brought forth from it descendants black like specks, and said: "O Adam, these are your descendants." Then He said to them: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: "Yes." He said to the white ones: "These are for Paradise by My mercy, and I do not mind," and they are the companions of the right hand. He said to the black ones: "These are for the Fire, and I do not mind," and they are the companions of the left hand. Then He returned them all into his loins, so the dwellers of the graves are held back until all the people of the covenant come forth from the loins of men and the wombs of women.

Allah, may He be exalted, said concerning those who broke the covenant: ﴿And We found most of them not faithful to covenant﴾. Abu al-Aliyah related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b concerning this verse that he said: Allah gathered them all together, made them spirits, then formed them, then made them speak, and said: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: "Yes, we bear witness that You are our Lord and our God; there is no lord for us besides You." Allah, may He be exalted, said: "I will send My messengers to you and reveal My books to you, so do not deny My messengers, and affirm My words, for I will surely take vengeance upon whoever associates partners with Me and does not believe in Me." Then He took their pledge and their covenant.

In some reports: Allah brought forth the descendants of Adam, scattered them before Adam, then spoke to them directly (qubulan), i.e., face to face (ayanan), and said: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ They said: "Yes." It was also said: He gave them intellects with which they understand, and tongues with which they speak, then addressed them and inspired them with the answer.

Some exegetes related from the scholars of the early generations: all of them said "Yes," but the believers said "Yes" willingly, while the disbelievers said it unwillingly. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly﴾.

We return to His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾. If someone says: Since the extraction was from the back of Adam, how did He say: "took from the Children of Adam, from their loins"? Some scholars answered this: Allah, may He be exalted, extracted them from the loins of Adam in the order in which He brings them forth from the children of Adam until the Day of Resurrection. Therefore He said: ﴿took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾.

Know that the Mu'tazilah interpreted this verse, saying: it means the taking from the backs of the children of Adam in the order in which the sunnah has passed from Adam until the end of the world.

As for His saying: ﴿and made them testify concerning themselves﴾, it means, as He set up the proofs of reason that indicate His being Lord, and compelled them to answer with their saying "Yes"; and they denied the covenant. This is a false interpretation. As for the People of the Sunnah, they affirm the Day of the Covenant, and the verse is as previously mentioned.

﴿And He made them testify concerning themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes, we testify, lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: Indeed we were unaware of this﴾. They differed concerning His saying: ﴿we testify﴾. Some said: this is from the speech of Allah and the angels, who said: "We testify." It was also said: it is the speech of those addressed, who said: "Yes, we testify." And it was said: there is an ellipsis, and its meaning is: Allah, may He be exalted, said to the angels: "Bear witness," and they said: "We bear witness."

As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection﴾, it is read with the letter ya' and with the letter ta'. Whoever reads with ya', the sense of the speech is: "And He made them testify concerning themselves so that they would not say on the Day of Resurrection: Indeed we were unaware of this." Whoever reads with ta', the sense of the speech is: "I address you: Am I not your Lord? So that you do not say on the Day of Resurrection: Indeed we were unaware of this." If someone says: The proof only binds in this world when they turn away from that covenant, which was on the Day of the Covenant, and which no one remembers, so that by turning away one becomes a rebel, and the proof then binds him. It was also said: Allah, may He be exalted, has made the evidences clear and set them up for His oneness, and confirmed His saying, and He has informed about the Day of the Covenant, and He is truthful in His reports; so whoever breaks that covenant is a rebel, and the proof clings to him.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Or [lest] you say, "It was only our fathers who associated partners with Allah before, and we were [merely] offspring after them. Will You then destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾

He means: I took what I took of the covenant and the pledge from you all, so that you would not say: ﴿It was only our fathers who associated partners with Allah before, and we were offspring after them﴾. That is, the wrongdoing belongs to the fathers, and we were only followers of them; so they would make for themselves a proof and an excuse before Allah. In this there is evidence that the children of the disbelievers are with the disbelievers.

﴿Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?﴾ That is: will You punish us for the wrongdoing of our misguided fathers?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 174:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We detail the verses, that perhaps they may return.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 175:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And recite to them the news of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Masʿud said: it refers to Balaam ibn Baʿura, and it is said: Balaam ibn Baʿir. He was in the city of the giants, and he had with him the Greatest Name (al-ism al-aʿzam). When Moses came against them with his army, they said to Balaam: "Moses is a man of fierce temper, so pray to Allah that He turn Moses away from us." It is also said: their king invited him to himself and said this to him, and Balaam said: "If I did that, my religion and my worldly life would be gone." They kept pressing him until he prayed to Allah, the Exalted, and his prayer was answered, and Moses was turned away from them, and He caused them to fall into the wandering (al-tih). When they fell into the wandering, Moses said: "O Lord, why have You imprisoned us in the wandering?" He said: "Because of the prayer of Balaam." Moses said: "O Allah, just as You answered his prayer against us, answer my prayer against him." Then he prayed to Allah, the Exalted, that He would strip him of the Greatest Name and of faith, and He did so. It is also said: Allah stripped him of the Greatest Name and of faith, as a punishment for what he had prayed for, and that was not by the prayer of Moses. This is the meaning of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿but he detached himself from them﴾.

ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs said: the verse refers to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi, who sought religion before the Prophet's mission, and who hoped that he would be a prophet. When the Prophet was sent, he envied him and disbelieved in him. Umayya was a man of wisdom and fine admonition.

al-Hasan said: the verse refers to the hypocrites among the Jews. Mujahid said: the verse refers to a prophet among the prophets whom Allah sent to his people, and his people bribed him. This is the weakest of the sayings, because Allah protects His prophets from such things. And from Ibn ʿAbbas, in another narration, that the verse refers to a man from the Children of Israel who had three answered supplications which Allah had granted him. He had an ugly wife, and she said to him: "Pray to Allah that He make me the most beautiful of the women of the world." He prayed to Allah and his prayer was answered; then she became arrogant and disobedient toward him, so he prayed to Allah that He make her a dog, and she became one. Then her sons said to him: "Pray to Allah that He return her," and he prayed to Allah and she returned as she had been. So his three supplications were lost. The first two sayings are more apparent.

As for His words: ﴿Then Satan pursued him﴾, meaning: Satan overtook him. It is said: "tabiʿahu" when one travels in his tracks, and "atbaʿahu" when one overtakes him. ﴿So he was among the misguided﴾, meaning: among those who went astray.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 176:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby﴾, meaning: We would have raised his rank and status through those verses and caused him to die before he disbelieved. It is also said that the meaning is: Had We willed, We would have placed [a barrier] between him and disbelief. ﴿But he inclined toward the earth﴾, meaning: he leaned toward this world, ﴿and followed his desire﴾. This is the most severe verse concerning the scholars, for a scholar is rarely free of one of these two: inclining toward the world, or following his desires.

﴿So his likeness is that of the dog: if you drive it away, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants﴾. He was given a parable of the basest animal in the basest condition, for he was likened to a dog panting. The real meaning is: if you chase the dog away, it pants, and if you leave it, it pants. Likewise the disbeliever: if you admonish and rebuke him, he is astray, and if you leave him, he is astray. Al-lahth (panting) is the hanging out of the tongue.

﴿That is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs﴾. The parable was given, and then it was made clear that it is the likeness of those (who) were previously mentioned. It is also said: all of this is a parable for the disbelievers of Makkah, for they used to wish that a prophet would come from among them. When the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, they envied him and disbelieved; thus they were disbelievers before his mission and disbelievers (after his mission). ﴿So relate the stories, that perhaps they may reflect.﴾
God Most High says: ﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾. That is, "wretched is the example of the people" (﴿and themselves they used to wrong﴾).

"Whoever Allah guides" — that is, whom Allah guides: ﴿Then he is the one guided﴾, and whoever He leaves astray — that is, whom Allah leaves astray: ﴿then those are the losers﴾. And this is evidence against the Qadariyya (the Qadariyya, an early school that denied God's predetermination of human acts), inasmuch as it attributes guidance and misguidance to His action without any cause.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 179:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾. That is: We created many for Hell. This is in accordance with the statement of the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah). ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed Allah, may He be exalted, created Paradise and created for it its people; He created them for it while they were in the loins of their fathers. And He created the Fire and created for it its people; He created them for it while they were in the loins of their fathers." This is in the Sahih. In another narration: "Indeed Allah, may He be exalted, created Paradise and created for it people by their names, the names of their fathers, and the names of their tribes. And He created the Fire and created for it people by their names, the names of their fathers, and the names of their tribes" — and this hadith is not in the Sahih — "none is added to them and none is subtracted from them."

It has also been said that the meaning of His saying ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell﴾ is: We created them, and the final outcome of their affair is toward Hell, and the lam is the lam of consequence (lam al-ʿaqibah). This is like the saying of the poet:

(O Umm Sulaym, do not be dismayed... for death is what the mother bears)

And another said:

(And for death the mothers raise their young, just as for the ruin of time the dwellings are built)

The first view is more correct and closer to the position of the People of the Sunnah. As for His saying: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand, and they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear﴾, its meaning is: since they did not comprehend with their hearts what would benefit them, and did not see with their eyes, and did not hear with their ears, what would benefit them, it is as if they do not understand, do not see, and do not hear anything at all. This is like the saying of Miskin al-Darimi:

(I am blind when my neighbour appears, until my neighbour is hidden by the curtain)

(Deaf to what passes between us is my hearing, and there is no deafness in the hearing)

﴿Those are like cattle﴾, meaning: in that their concern in this world is eating and enjoying desires. ﴿Nay, they are more astray﴾, because cattle distinguish between harm and benefit, whereas those do not distinguish what harms them from what benefits them. ﴿Those are the heedless﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 180:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to God belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them﴾. "The most beautiful names" (al-asma' al-husna) are those that have come in the report (khabar). Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed God has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever counts them enters Paradise." His saying "the most beautiful" refers to the names (al-tasmiyat), and His saying ﴿so call upon Him by them﴾ means that one says: "O Mighty (ya 'Aziz), O Merciful (ya Rahman)," and the like of this.

Know that the names of God Most High are by revelation only (tawqif). He is named "Generous" (jawad) but is not named "Bountiful" (sakhi), even though it has the meaning of "generous." He is named "Merciful" (rahim) but is not named "tender-hearted" (raqiq). He is named "Knowing" ('alim) but is not named "Intelligent" ('aqil). On this basis, one does not say: "O Deceiver (ya khadi')," "O Schemer (ya makkar)," even though they occur in the Qur'an (﴿They seek to deceive God, but He is the One who deceives them﴾, and ﴿they scheme and God schemes﴾). But since the Law has not come with naming Him by them, it is not permissible for Him.

His saying: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾. Ya'qub ibn al-Sikkit, author of al-Islah, said: al-ilhad (deviation) is inclining away from the truth and introducing what is not part of the religion. It was said: deviation concerning the names here means that they used to say, in opposition to God's name, "al-Lat," and in opposition to "al-'Aziz," "al-'Uzza," and "Manat" in opposition to "al-Mannan." It was also said: it is their naming of idols as gods, and this is the greatest deviation concerning the names. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names; they will be recompensed for what they used to do﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 181:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And among those whom We created is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice.﴾ Qatadah narrated as a mursal report from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "These are from this community, and such (people) existed among those before you." He pointed by this to the people of Musa (Moses), just as the Most High said: ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community who guide by the truth and by it do justice.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 182:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who deny Our signs, We will draw them on step by step from where they do not know.﴾ Al-Azhari said: Istidraj (gradual drawing-on, step-by-step leading) is taking [someone] little by little, and from it comes the word "darraja al-kitab" (he rolled up the scroll, i.e., gradually folded it, from the same root). It was also said: istidraj from Allah is that whenever the servant increases in disobedience, Allah, may He be exalted, increases him in blessings. It was also said: it is that blessings are abundantly bestowed upon him and he is made to forget gratitude, and then He seizes him suddenly. This is the istidraj "from where they do not know."
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And I give them respite﴾, meaning: I grant them time and delay them. ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾, meaning: strong.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 184:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion; he is only a clear warner.﴾ The occasion of revelation of this verse is what has been narrated: "That the Prophet, one night, climbed al-Safa and was calling all night long: O children of so-and-so, O children of so-and-so, indeed I am a warner to you before a severe punishment. When they woke in the morning, they said: Indeed Muhammad has gone mad; he shouts all night long. So this verse was revealed." ﴿Have they not reflected?﴾ meaning: concerning the state of Muhammad, that madness does not befit his condition.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 185:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not considered the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ He means: let them take them as evidence for the oneness of God, may He be exalted. ﴿And [have they not considered] what God has created of any thing?﴾ That is: have they not looked at what God has created of any thing? ﴿And that it may be that their term has drawn near﴾ He means: perhaps their term has drawn near, so that they die before they believe. ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ That is: in what prophet after Muhammad, and in what book after the book of Muhammad, will they believe?

Almost literal translation with markers kept.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Whomever God leaves astray﴾, meaning: whomever God leaves astray, ﴿there is no guide for him. And He leaves them in their rebellion, wandering blindly﴾, meaning: in their excess in falsehood, ﴿wandering blindly﴾, bewildered and hesitating.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 187:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it take place?﴾ That is, when will it be established (mursa). It is said: arsa, meaning: athbata (he established/fixed it). Its meaning: they ask you about the Hour, when will its establishment occur. ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal it at its time﴾, meaning: none will manifest it at its time ( ﴿except He﴾ it lies heavy upon the heavens and the earth). That is: its knowledge is hidden within the heavens and the earth, and so it is as if it were heavy, and everything hidden is heavy. Its meaning: its description is heavy upon the people of the heavens and the earth, because of what will happen in it: the folding up of the sun and the moon, the folding up of the stars, the moving of the mountains, and the rolling up of the heavens and the earth. It is also said its meaning: its occurrence will be grievous upon the people of the heavens and the earth.

﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly.

﴿They ask you as if you were eager about it﴾. That is, as if you were pleased by their asking about it. It is said: tahaffaytu fulanan fi al-mas'ala, when you ask someone persistently about a matter and show delight in your asking. So according to this, the verse's estimate is: they ask you about it as if you were pleased by their asking. It is also said its meaning: they ask you as if you were knowledgeable about it (hafiyy 'anha), meaning: aware of it. It is said: ahfaytu fulanan, when you press someone much in a question until you know. So according to this, the meaning of the verse is: as if you had pressed much in asking about it, until you knew. ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with God, but most people do not know﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 188:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: I possess no power to benefit myself or to harm myself, except as Allah wills. Had I known the unseen, I would have acquired abundance of good, and no harm would have touched me.﴾ Concerning it there are three opinions:

The first: its meaning is: "Had I known prosperity from drought, I would have stored up from the years of plenty for the years of drought, and hunger would not have touched me." This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jurayj said: its meaning is: "Had I known when I would die, I would have acquired abundance of good deeds and acts of obedience, and no harm (al-su') would have touched me," i.e., there is no madness in me, for they had attributed madness to him.

The third opinion: its meaning is: "Had I known when the Hour would come, I would have informed you of its establishment so that you might believe, and no harm (al-su') would have touched me," meaning: from your denial. ﴿I am but a warner and a bringer of good tidings for a people who believe.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 189:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿He it is who created you from a single soul﴾, meaning Adam, ﴿and made from it its mate﴾, meaning Hawwa' (Eve), ﴿that he might dwell with her﴾. ﴿When he covered her﴾, that is, had intercourse with her. Covering (al-ghashayan) is the most beautiful metaphor (kinayah) for intercourse. It is said: "He covered her and penetrated her," meaning he had intercourse with her.

﴿She bore a light burden﴾: this is the first thing a woman carries from the drop (nutfah). ﴿And she went about with it﴾. Yahya ibn Ya'mar recited: "fa-marrat bihi" with a light (khafif) pronunciation, from al-miyah (doubt), meaning she doubted. In the irregular readings (al-shawadhdh) it is recited "fa-mara bihi" (fa-marat), meaning she moved with it, from al-maur (movement). Ibn 'Abbas recited "fa-istamarrat bihi," and this is the meaning of the well-known recitation. Its meaning is: she went about with the pregnancy until she stood up, sat down, entered and exited. It is also said that it is inverted (maqlub), and its original form is: the pregnancy went about with her until she stood up and sat down. ﴿When she became heavy﴾, that is, the time of delivery arrived. ﴿They both called upon Allah, their Lord﴾.

In the narrative: Iblis came to Hawwa' when she became pregnant and said to her: "Do you know what is in your belly?" She said: "No." He said: "Perhaps it is an animal, and I fear it may have two horns with which it will split your belly." Hawwa' became frightened and sat down, grieved. Then the accursed one returned to her and said: "Do you want me to call upon Allah, the Exalted, that He make it a speaking human?" She said: "Yes." He said: "I have already whispered to you both once, so obey me until I call upon Him." She said: "What should we do?" The accursed one said: "When you give birth, name him Abd al-Harith," for the name of Iblis had previously been al-Harith. She mentioned that to Adam, and they agreed upon it. When she gave birth, they named him Abd al-Harith. It is also said: she gave birth once and they named him Abd Allah, and he died. Then she gave birth to another child and they named him Abd Allah, and he died. The accursed one came and said: "Do you not know that Allah, the Exalted, does not leave His servant with you? When you give birth to a child, name him Abd al-Harith, so that he lives." When she gave birth to the third, they named him Abd al-Harith, and he lived and survived.

In a report: the Prophet said: "Iblis deceived them both twice: once in Paradise and once on earth," and he meant this.

The words ﴿When she became heavy, they both called upon Allah, their Lord﴾, meaning Adam and Hawwa', ﴿saying: If You give us a righteous one﴾, that is, a child other than the creation, since they were both [supplicating] that Allah make him a human like them, out of fear of the whispering of Iblis. ﴿We will surely be among the thankful.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 190:

﴿So when He gave them a righteous (child)﴾, i.e., sound in form (sawiyy al-khalq), ﴿they made for Him partners in what He had given them﴾, meaning they named him ʿAbd al-Harith.

If someone says: how can He say ﴿they made for Him partners﴾ when Adam was a prophet protected (maʿsum) from associating others with God?

It is said: this was not shirk in tawhid (monotheism). Rather, it was shirk in naming (shirk fi al-ism), and that does not detract from tawhid. It is like a man naming his child ʿAbd Yaghuth, ʿAbd Zayd, or ʿAbd ʿAmr, and a man saying to his companion, "I am your slave" (ʿabduka). Upon this is the statement of Yusuf, peace be upon him: ﴿Indeed, He is my Lord; He has made my residence excellent﴾. Such things do not detract (from tawhid). As for His saying ﴿Exalted is God above what they associate﴾, it is a new statement after the first, and by it He intended the associating of the people of Makkah. And if He intended by it the shirk that preceded, the speech would be consistent, since it would have been better that they not do what they did of shirk in naming, and that was a slip (zallah) on their part; therefore He said ﴿Exalted is God above what they associate﴾.

There is another view regarding the verse: that this refers to all the children of Adam. ʿIkrimah said: "It is as if God addresses each one of the creation with His saying ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul﴾, meaning, He created each one from his father, ﴿and made from it its mate﴾, i.e., made from its kind its mate, ﴿that he might dwell in tranquility with her﴾, meaning, each husband with his wife, ﴿then when he covered her﴾, i.e., had intercourse with her, ﴿she bore a light burden and carried it about﴾." And this is a good view regarding the verse.

It is also said: the reference to Adam and Eve is a way of speaking about all their offspring, because they are the origin of all. The first view is more well-known and more apparent, and it is the statement of Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr. And the group of exegetes all said: the verse is about Adam and Eve, as we have explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 191:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do they associate with Him those who create nothing and are themselves created?﴾ He means: the idols create nothing; rather, they are themselves created.
﴿And they are unable to help them, nor can they help themselves.﴾ That is: protection (*man'an*).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 193:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you.﴾ This refers to specific people whom God knew would not believe. ﴿It is the same for you whether you call them or you remain silent.﴾ That is: it is the same whether you call them or do not call them; they will not believe.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 194:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah are servants like you﴾. If someone asks: How can the idols be servants like us? It is said: Muqatil said: By this He meant the angels, and the address is to a people who used to worship the angels. And it is said: He meant by it the devils (shayatin), and the address is to a people who used to worship soothsayers (kahana) and the devils. The correct view is that it refers to the idols, and they are servants like people in worship, and their worship is glorification (tasbih). The inanimate things also have glorification, as the Book has declared: ﴿And there is not a thing but it glorifies [Allah] by His praise﴾. His words ﴿like you﴾ mean: the idols are subjected and made subservient to what is wanted from them, like you. This is like His words, the Exalted: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies with its wings, but they are communities like you﴾, and its meaning is: like you in some respects and not in others. So also here. It is also said: He only said ﴿like you﴾ because they fashioned them in the form of living beings and asked of them what is asked of living beings.

﴿So invoke them, and let them respond to you, if you are truthful﴾. This is to demonstrate their incapacity. Then He emphasized it, saying:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 195:

﴿Do they have feet with which they walk? Or do they have hands with which they strike? Or do they have eyes with which they see? Or do they have ears with which they hear?﴾ That is because the power of created beings is only exercised through these instruments and limbs, and those instruments are not theirs. Rather, you have greater power than they do, since these things exist in you.

﴿Say: Call upon your associates, then scheme against me, and give me no respite.﴾ That is: do not grant me a reprieve.

Allah the Exalted says: (Indeed my guardian is Allah, who revealed the Book). That is, my helper and supporter is Allah, who revealed the Book. It is recited in the irregular readings (shawadh): "Inna waliyya Allah" with a kasra on the ha', and its meaning is: Jibril is the guardian of Allah, who revealed the Book, i.e., who brought down the Book. ﴿And He befriends the righteous﴾, that is, Jibril is the guardian of the righteous. This is like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah is his Protector, and Jibril﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 197:

His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.﴾ This is also to demonstrate their powerlessness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 198:

﴿And if you call them to guidance, they do not hear.﴾ He means: the idols. ﴿And you see them looking at you, but they do not see.﴾ If it is asked: how can looking be attributed to idols? Al-Kisa'i said: The Arabs say, "My house looks toward the house of so-and-so," when it faces it. Likewise His words, ﴿And you see them looking at you﴾, mean the looking of facing (nazar al-muqabalah).

The Qur'anic phrase: ﴿Take what is freely given, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant.﴾ He said: It is narrated that when Jibril, peace and blessings of God be upon him, descended with this verse, he said: "O Messenger of God, I have brought you the noblest of character traits." It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) asked Jibril about the meaning of this verse, and he said to him: "Let me ask my Lord," then he returned and said: "Join ties with the one who cuts you off, give to the one who withholds from you, and pardon the one who wrongs you."

Then they differed regarding the meaning of this "pardon" (al-'afw). 'Ata' said: It is the surplus of people's wealth. In the beginning it was obligatory to give in charity whatever exceeded one's needs, and then it was abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of an earlier ruling by a later one) by the verse of zakat (obligatory almsgiving). This is the meaning of His words, ﴿They ask you what they should spend. Say: the surplus.﴾ Ibn al-Zubayr said: al-'Afw is what is easily available of people's character, meaning: take what is easy from people's characters, such as accepting apologies, pardoning and being lenient in matters, leaving off probing into things, and the like.

As for His words, ﴿and enjoin what is good﴾, it is the enjoining of what is good (al-ma'ruf), which is what the Shari'ah recognizes.

As for His words, ﴿and turn away from the ignorant﴾, it means: if the ignorant person behaves foolishly toward you, do not requite him and do not respond to him with foolishness. This is like His words, ﴿When the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace,"﴾ meaning the peace of disengagement. He said: ﴿When they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity,﴾ meaning they honor themselves by refraining from engaging in it.

It is narrated that 'Uyayna ibn Hisn, who was the chief of Ghatafan, when he came to Madina, said to al-Hurr ibn Qays: "You have standing with the Commander of the Faithful, so ask permission for me to see him." So he asked permission for him, and he entered upon 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, and said to him: "You do not judge among us with truth, nor do you distribute among us with justice." 'Umar became angry and intended to harm him, but al-Hurr ibn Qays said: "God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And turn away from the ignorant,﴾ and this man is among the ignorant." So 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, fell silent.

The Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah﴾. Al-nazgh (the prompting, a slight incitement) from Satan is whispering (al-waswasa). ﴿Then seek refuge in Allah﴾, meaning: seek protection (istajir) in Allah. ﴿Indeed He is Hearing, Knowing﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 201:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse (ṭayf) from Satan touches them﴾. It is also read "ṭā'if," and both have the same meaning.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is anger. Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: it is whispering (waswasah). The root of ṭayf is madness (junun).

﴿They remember, and then they are seeing clearly﴾. Regarding its meaning there are two opinions. The first: when Satan whispers to them with disobedience, they remember the punishment of Allah, and then they refrain from disobedience.

The second opinion: its meaning is that they remember Allah, and then they see the truth from falsehood clearly.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 202:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And their brothers﴾, meaning: their likes among the devils, ﴿continue to drive them﴾, meaning: they drive them back ﴿into error﴾, into misguidance, ﴿and then they do not hold back﴾, meaning: they do not desist.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when you do not bring them a sign, they say, "Why have you not fabricated one?"﴾ They used to ask the Prophet for signs, testing him (ta'annutan) and multiplying their requests for them. So when he did not recite a sign to them, they would say, "Why have you not chosen it?" That is: "Why did you not invent it and say it from yourself?" He said: ﴿Say, "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. This is insight from your Lord, and guidance and mercy for a people who believe."﴾ It means: the Qur'an."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 204:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy.﴾ Al-Hasan, al-Zuhri and al-Nakha'i said: This refers to recitation during the prayer. ʿAṭāʾ and Mujahid said: It refers to the khutba (sermon). But Mujahid's view was not accepted, because the verse is Meccan, whereas the Friday prayer was only made obligatory in Medina; and because listening throughout the entire khutba is obligatory, so it is not restricted to the recitation within the khutba. Therefore the first view is more sound.

As for those who hold that one should not recite behind the imam, there is no valid proof for them in this verse, because reciting behind the imam does not contradict listening, since the follower pauses in the imam's pauses; and because the verse concerns what comes after al-Fatiha, as shown by the hadith of ʿUbada ibn al-Samit, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "When you are behind me, do not recite anything except Umm al-Qur'an (al-Fatiha)."

There is a third view regarding the verse: that it means a prohibition against speaking during the prayer. This was said by Abu Hurayra, and it is a good view.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 7, verse 205:

The words of the Most High, ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and with fear﴾. It was said: this refers to supplication, meaning: call upon God with humility and fear. And it was said: it refers to the silent prayer (salat al-sirr).

.

﴿And without loudness in speech﴾: he intended by this: in the loud prayer, do not recite with excessive loudness. ﴿In the mornings and the evenings﴾. So al-ghuduww (the morning) is the early part of the day, and al-asal (the evenings) is the latter part of the day. ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾, of the remembrance of God.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 7, verse 206:

The Most High said: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ means: the angels. He mentioned them with nearness and honour. ﴿They do not disdain from His worship, and they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate﴾. Meaning: if these (people) disdain from worshipping God Most High, then those who are with Him do not disdain from it.

Traditions about prostration (sujud) have been transmitted, among them: what Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When the son of Adam prostrates, Satan withdraws weeping and says, 'Woe is me! The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate, and he prostrated, so he will have Paradise; and I was commanded to prostrate, and I refused, so I will have the Fire.'"

In the hadith of Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b al-Aslami: he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with his water for his need, and the Prophet said, "Ask me." I said, "I want to be your companion in Paradise." He said, "Or is there anything other than that?" I said, "That is it." He said, "Then help me against your own self by much prostration." Related by Muslim in the Sahih.

Abu Fatimah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "No servant prostrates to Allah a single prostration except that Allah raises him by it one degree." And Allah knows best.
